title: Takeaways from Cardinals vs. Raiders, including three quarterbacks
summary: Any win is a good win. But the Arizona Cardinals’ victory in an exhibition game against the Las Vegas Raiders was costly, as they lost their star rookie offensive guard, Chase Bisontis, who will have surgery next week. As a fan, you may be inclined to utter that maybe head coach Mike LaFleur shouldn’t play […]
full_text: WR Simi Fehoko #80 and QB Gardner Minshew #15 (Photo by Ian Maule/Getty Images) | Getty Images Any win is a good win. But the Arizona Cardinals’ victory in an exhibition game against the Las Vegas Raiders was costly, as they lost their star rookie offensive guard, Chase Bisontis, who will have surgery next week. Red Sea representing ♥️ @CoxComm | #RiseUpRedSea pic.twitter.com/u7jFm9GTzo — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 As a fan, you may be inclined to utter that maybe head coach Mike LaFleur shouldn’t play any starters in any of the preseason games in order to not lose players. Except Bisontis was playing with the second string, not the starting unit. Yeah – that. RELATED: CARDINALS GET FIRST WIN OF PRESEASON Second verse same as the first. The coaching staff has to know who to cut, and these games will tell that story most of the time. Some really good players have balled out in the past and became the preseason darling, and yet were released or didn’t start as expected. With the Raiders game, several takeaways did not make the Beaks & Geek and other post-game articles. Here goes: ————————————————————————————————————————- Jacoby Brissett looked established, Gardner Minshew appeared competent, and Kedon Slovis was eyeballed as one to trust All of the game’s quarterbacks looked really good. All game. Jacoby → Marv 🔁🔁🔁 📲 on NFL+ pic.twitter.com/0DB4EXhc4g — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 Brissett was the biggest question mark, but marched the team down the field, made good throws when needed, and relied on his running game with both RBs Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier. The third-and-11 toss to WR Michael Wilson was an excellent throw that kept the drive going. The touchdown throw to the back corner of the end zone to WR Marv Harrison was highlight-reel stuff. MINSHEW TO SIMI FOR SIX! 📲 NFL+ pic.twitter.com/ifOdeHVoc9 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 After that first drive, Minshew carried the torch. Literally. He looked like a Week 1 starter and has this offense down already. His first two possessions were an 11-play drive for 78 yards and a 10-play drive for 75 yards. Both ended in touchdowns. He used Love as both a runner and a short-gain receiver, and it worked. Nice 9-yard toss to WR Jalen Brooks, plus the touchdown thrown to WR Simi Fehoko, was on the money. Minshew hit Brooks again in the second drive for 14 and 10 yards, like the pair were college teammates. Then Minshew came out of the halftime tunnel and guided the team to a 10-play drive that ended in three points. Final outing: three drives, 17 points. Slovis came in late in the third quarter and finished the game against a lot of second-team talent and some third-stringers. He was on point with his passes. You may say, “Well, that’s against the Raiders’ third-string guys,” which is true, but a throw to a small window exists at all levels. You still have to throw it, and Slovis did. His first drive ended in three points. The guys are too hyped for Jalen Brooks 🥹 pic.twitter.com/7nqf2865mo — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 Receivers are the bomb The Cardinals receivers are killing it. From Wilson and Harrison to the veteran Fehoko to the new guys, this group is something. Brooks continues to impress and is making his claim to end up on the main roster. The rookie Reggie Virgil also has shown promise with a sensational 19-yard grab in the fourth quarter. Kendrick Bourne should start in the slot, which leaves seven good receivers to fight it out for three spots. Walter Nolen bullied his way to the sack 💪 pic.twitter.com/IrKmIpZKI0 — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 14, 2026 Where was the pass rush? Um, we know Josh Sweat isn’t playing in the preseason. But the remainder of the defensive line group should be fighting for jobs. DT Walter Nolen didn’t play many reps, but he got penetration into the offensive backfield with a sack and a QB hit. DT Roy Lopez played good run defense, but nothing deep. Zaven Collins, B.J. Ojulari, and L.J. Collier? The coaches have praised DE Darius Robinson, who ended up with zero stats. The side opposite Sweat has got to find a consistent pass rush. Special teams are certainly special K Chad Ryland missed his first field goal of the preseason, but he is collectively 4-for-5 and nailed a 56-yarder. P Blake Gillikin is an amazing punter and isn’t getting those 60+ kicks, but has consistent depth numbers. The new long snapper, Casey Kreiter, is laying his passes right where Gillikin wants the ball in order to kick his kicks off fast. Special Teams Coordinator Michael Ghobrial is still shuffling in punt and kickoff returners. With kickoff, he used WR Ihmir Smith-Marsette for a 24-yard return, then WR Devin Duvernay for a 21-yard return. It is assumed that Duvernay’s job on this roster is to return both types of kicks. He returned one punt for eight yards while Smith-Marsette returned a punt for four yards. Defenders who are showing out The rookie LB Karson Sharar led all defenders with five tackles, but he was everywhere. Good speed to the ball. Another linebacker, Jack Gibbens, looked great in coverage and has been reading the run well, then finding his gap. A guy who has looked exceptional in both preseason games is CB Elijah Jones. He had four tackles and has been a shadow to whichever receiver he has taken. The Cardinals will keep six cornerbacks, with Will Johnson, Denzel Burke, and Garrett Williams a lock. Max Melton should make it, and perhaps Sean Murphy-Bunting? Maybe? 11 corners on the roster presently. Play calling The team we as Cardinals fans should be sending condolence greeting cards to is the Detroit Lions. They ended up with Drew Petzing as their OC, their play caller, and their architect of an already good offensive group. Arizona now has LaFleur, and he is creative. And think about it: This is just a vanilla version. You can’t show your hand early, and LaFleur has restrained himself, yet the offense is looking really good. 23 offensive first downs are such a positive sign. Was 8-for-15 on third downs and 1-for-1 on the fourth-down situation. That is being aggressive. Plus, Arizona’s offense was on the field nine minutes more than the Raiders. If the Cardinals can control the clock and time of possession, that means the other team’s offense can’t score.

title: Falcons snap counts from a Week 1 preseason loss to the Broncos
summary: You’ve been itching for snap counts, and we have them! Here’s a breakdown of Friday night’s snaps, courtesy of Pro Football Focus. Offense WR Dylan Drummond: 39 RT/LT Mike Jerrell: 38 RG Brandon Walton: 35 WR Chris Blair: 31 LG Layden Robinson: 30 WR Zachariah Branch: 28 TE Jack Velling: 27 LG Kyle Hinton: 27 […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - AUGUST 14: Tyler Goodson #25 of the Atlanta Falcons rushes against Jahdae Barron #23 of the Denver Broncos during the second quarter of a NFL preseason game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on August 14, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images You’ve been itching for snap counts, and we have them! Here’s a breakdown of Friday night’s snaps, courtesy of Pro Football Focus . Offense WR Dylan Drummond: 39 RT/LT Mike Jerrell: 38 RG Brandon Walton: 35 WR Chris Blair: 31 LG Layden Robinson: 30 WR Zachariah Branch: 28 TE Jack Velling: 27 LG Kyle Hinton: 27 QB Cooper Rush: 27 C Corey Levin: 27 QB Jack Strand: 25 C James Brockermeyer: 25 RG Andrew Stueber: 25 HB Tyler Goodson: 24 G Kam Dewberry: 22 RT Ethan Onianwa: 22 WR Vinny Anthony: 20 RB Nate Carter: 15 LT Riley Mahlman: 13 WR Antwane Wells Jr.: 13 TE Josh Simon: 13 TE Nick Muse: 13 WR Kristian Wilkerson: 13 WR Keelan Marion: 12 RT Wanya Morris: 9 LG Matthew Bergeron: 8 WR Jahan Dotson: 8 TE Kyle Pitts: 8 HB Brian Robinson: 8 RG Chris Lindstrom: 8 C Ryan Neuzil: 8 RB Cash Jones: 7 RB Trey Sermon: 6 WR Olamide Zaccheaus: 6 TE Austin Hooper: 5 LT Jake Matthews: 3 WR Drake London: 2 TE Charlie Woerner: 2 It was a long, long look for Dylan Drummond and Chris Blair as is typical, and Blair looked good again. There were also long looks at several offensive linemen in this one, with Layden Robinson and and Kyle Hinton helping themselves and Mike Jerrell and Ethan Onianwa pretty emphatically not helping themselves. There was no magic performance on the offensive side of the ball that will make or break someone’s roster spot, though Goodson thoroughly outperforming the other backs he’s competing with certainly is going to give him an early leg up. Though he only played 13 snaps, I’d also say Josh Simon had the kind of performance that ought to help him push for a potential fourth tight end spot. Simon looked good as a blocker and really strong as a receiver, flashing good hands and proving to be tough for Denver’s reserves to tackle. He’ll have to build on that, but this tight end depth chart could use another developmental pass catcher with Charlie Woerner and Austin Hooper on expiring deals, and Simon was intriguing a year ago. Other than that, the less we saw about the quarterback, the better. At least we saw a handful of zippy balls between Jack Strand and Cooper Rush. Defense DL Devonnsha Maxwell: 43 CB Cobee Bryant: 40 ILB Josh Woods: 38 S DeMarcco Hellams: 37 S Sydney Brown: 37 CB CJ Henderson: 37 DL Carlos Allen: 36 DL Chris Williams: 36 CB Clark Phillips: 33 CB A.J. Woods: 32 CB Darren Hall: 32 DL Marlon Tuipolotu: 32 OLB Azeez Ojulari: 30 S Jammie Robinson: 28 ILB JD Bertrand: 26 ILB Kendal Daniels: 25 OLB Cameron Thomas: 24 OLB Keshawn Banks: 24 OLB Cam Sample: 23 OLB James Pearce Jr.: 22 CB Malcolm DeWalt IV: 20 ILB Harold Perkins Jr.: 20 DL Zach Harrison: 20 CB Darnay Holmes: 19 ILB Christian Harris: 17 OLB Samson Ebukam: 17 CB Mike Hughes: 14 ILB Daveren Rayner: 12 S Keidron Smith: 12 ILB Channing Tindall: 12 DL Maason Smith: 11 DL Brandon Dorlus: 6 CB A.J. Terrell: 6 CB Mike Ford: 4 For some defenders, the extended look was a good thing. Devonnsha Maxwell made the most of his team-leading snaps with some solid pass rush reps, Josh Woods looking physical and active as always, and Sydney Brown put forward the type of well-rounded performance that will help him stick around as a versatile. Rookies Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins Jr. were really impressive, I thought, given that both were drawing major snaps for the first time in their NFL snaps. While they didn’t get as many snaps, DeWalt and Banks also stood out to me with strong days on defense. All of these players made headway in their respective battles, and for Maxwell, DeWalt, and Banks, these kinds of days could mean a practice squad spot. Things were a little less sunny for Cobee Bryant, who is far too talented to struggle as much as he did against Denver, with a missed tackle and three of four targets headed his way ending up complete. Bryant has a lot of competition for a role in 2026, and while I think the Falcons like him enough that he’ll at least have a practice squad spot sewn up, there’s too many useful players in the competition for him to have another effort like that. For what it’s worth, I’m pretty confident he won’t. The lack of pass rush production was concerning overall, but maybe especially so because the Falcons had James Pearce Jr. out there and couldn’t get the job done, something that won’t be true the first eight weeks of the season. Terrell: 1 Olamide Zaccheaus: 1 Brandon Walton: 1 Mike Hughes: 1 Kristian Wilkerson: 1 Samson Ebukam: 1 Leading the team in special teams snaps and playing well on offense is about as good as it gets for a roster hopeful at running back, so good for Goodson. The fact that special teams was by far Atlanta’s best unit bodes well for those players leading the way, with DeWalt’s standout night helping his chances and players like Bertrand and Josh Woods making fresh impressions on a new coaching staff.

According to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson, the Ravens signed veteran Jonathan Ward on Sunday. Ward is a five-year veteran who has played for four teams in the NFL thus far. He […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - OCTOBER 13: Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jonathan Ward (35) walks off the field after a NFL game between the Pittsburgh Steelers a d the Las Vegas Raiders on October 13, 2024, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images On the morning after a victory over the Philadelphia Eagles in their 2026 preseason opener, the Baltimore Ravens have reportedly made a running back addition. According to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson , the Ravens signed veteran Jonathan Ward on Sunday. #Ravens news: signed veteran running back Jonathan Ward today, per a league source @KPRC2 — Aaron Wilson (@AaronWilson_NFL) August 16, 2026 Ward is a five-year veteran who has played for four teams in the NFL thus far. He was originally signed by the Arizona Cardinals in 2020 as an undrafted free agent out of Central Michigan. After playing 32 games for the Cardinals, Ward joined the Tennessee Titans for two years and appeared in four games for the Pittsburgh Steelers in 2024. The 28-year-old running back has only 22 rushing attempts for his career with 91 rushing yards, along with another 52 receiving yards a touchdown. Ward was previously a very productive college player, totaling 3,446 scrimmage yards and 32 scores in four seasons at Central Michigan. The Ravens are already set at running back with Derrick Henry, Justice Hill, Rasheen Ali and Adam Randall all likely to be on the regular season roster. Ali suffered an injury earlier this week in practice, though, which sidelined him for consecutive practice sessions and Saturday’s preseason game. The signing of Ward could signal the Ravens expect Ali to continue to miss some time and thus need another running back to take snaps. In their win over the Eagles, Randall led the team in rushing with 46 yards and a touchdown. Undrafted rookies Elijah Tau-Tolliver and Donte McMillan combined for 19 carries and 82 yards on the ground. Henry and Hill are unlikely to see any preseason action, so expect Ward to join this group as a candidate to receive playing time over the next couple weeks.

title: 5 takeaways from Bills win over Panthers in first preseason game
summary: The Buffalo Bills beat the Carolina Panthers 29-14 in the first preseason game inside the new Highmark Stadium on Saturday afternoon, and the score was not indicative of how thoroughly the Bills dominated. Staffer Sean Murphy wrote his stock up/stock down piece immediately following the victory. It’s very good. You should read it. These were […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 15: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady on the sideline during the first half against the Carolina Panthers at Highmark Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills beat the Carolina Panthers 29-14 in the first preseason game inside the new Highmark Stadium on Saturday afternoon, and the score was not indicative of how thoroughly the Bills dominated. Staffer Sean Murphy wrote his stock up/stock down piece immediately following the victory. It’s very good. You should read it. These were my takeaways from this convincing Bills win. Joe Brady and Jim Leonhard are going to bring it No one would’ve blamed Brady and Leonard for opting to go vanilla schematically in their first exhibition game at head coach and defensive coordinator respectively. The opposite was true against Carolina — and I gotta say, I loved it. Brady didn’t shy away from deep drops for Josh Allen, even calling a few under center play-action passes. On those five drop backs, Allen was 5-of-5 for 100 yards and a touchdown. Brady prioritized pushing the ball down the field too. Last season, Allen finished with his lowest average depth of target (aDOT) in his NFL career, at just 7.8 yards. Of course, we can’t draw distinct conclusions from the first preseason game alone, but Allen’s aDOT against the Panthers was 13.6 yards. And Buffalo’s three blitzes on 31 Bryce Young and Kenny Pickett drop backs did not indicate the complex nature of what Leonhard threw at Carolina’s quarterbacks. There were a smattering of pre-snap blitz looks followed by post-snap rotations up front that confused the Panthers offensive line and led to four sacks of the three Carolina quarterbacks and a mere 4.9 yards-per-attempt average through the air. It was close to as foot-on-the-gas as you’ll see an offensive and defensive coordinator in a preseason opener. So is Deone Walker The best player on the field in the Bills-Panthers preseason contest was the second-year defensive tackle, who looked ridiculously sleek despite probably still weighing somewhere in the 320s or 330s at 6’7”. On 10 snaps, Walker had two pressures, one sack, three tackles, and one tackle for loss. He was lightning off the snap and a bull in a china shop working his way through the interior of Carolina’s blocking unit. The 2025 fourth-round pick appeared on just over 47% of the defensive snaps in last year’s regular season, yet never hit the rookie wall, and made his presence felt in both of Buffalo’s playoff games with six tackles, four total pressures, and an interception. Walker is one of those top 1% of the top 1% type specimens, and on Saturday against Carolina he gave everyone the first notification of what the 22 year old is capable of at a new, slimmed down weight in his second professional season as the starting nose tackle in Leonard’s scheme. The Bills back seven has legitimate versatility for the first time in a while Every single coach in the NFL preaches versatility with his players. But hardly every team has it, based on the way it should be defined. Sure, a coordinator can place a safety in the slot. That doesn’t mean said safety is automatically versatile. Can he play both safety and defend the slot well ? If so, then he’s legitimately versatile. The Bills had a workhorse of a nickel in Taron Johnson for the bulk of the Sean McDermott era. He was versatile in that he could cover underneath at a high level and was completely unafraid to throw his weight around in the box as a run defender. In his prime, he was damn good. All-Pro good. But his size was always a hindrance to the Bills ceiling defensively. Now, the Bills have super-sudden Dee Alford as the classically built/skilled slot corner. And Jordan Hancock and Jalon Kilgore are two larger, explosive, and youthful safety-nickel hybrids who starred in this preseason opener and could very well give the Bills personnel-matching versatility in their back seven. Even rookie seventh-round pick Toriano Pride Jr. is being crossed trained on the outside and in the slot. Maxwell Hairston has the juice to condense inside if needed. While versatile wouldn’t be the first word I would use to describe the 6’2” / 203-pound rookie Kani Walker, possessing that type of size — and burgeoning playmaking skill — behind Christian Benford was simply missing from the past few years of the Bills defenses when the likes of Dane Jackson and Co. were needed in key moments as injury reinforcements. The plethora of plays made by Kilgore and Hancock together hint at what’s materializing for the Bills secondary by way of legitimate versatility. Lloyd Cushenberry could become a low-key vital free-agent signing In late March, a few weeks into 2026 NFL free agency, the Bills signed Cushenberry to a one-year contract. After two average-at-best seasons in Tennessee, it was easy to dismiss the signing as insignificant. But now, we wonder — will Connor McGovern be ready for Week 1 against the Houston Texans? He probably isn’t even sure right now after suffering a leg muscle strain in the Blue and Red Scrimmage last weekend. There’s a reasonable chance McGovern won’t be available for that regular-season opener against one of the most ferocious defensive lines in the NFL. It appears Cushenberry would slide into the starting center spot if McGovern can’t go at any stage of the season. And it’s rather luxurious for Brady to have a backup blocker with 80 games of starting experience who just so happens to have been LSU’s center during the magical 2019 season. Against the Panthers, Cushenberry rocked in pass protection — he did not allow a pressure on 10 pass-blocking snaps. It is worth nothing… he didn’t see Derrick Brown at the nose in this game. Cushenberry isn’t an All-Pro caliber type. But offensive lines are weak-link systems. One liability can ruin the performance of the entire group. And Cushenberry’s first showing in a Bills uniform, coupled with his familiarity with Brady, suggest he can be a glue guy up front who can help to keep the Bills super-sturdy line afloat if the injury keeps McGovern out for a relatively long stretch at the outset of the season.

(Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images On a picture-perfect afternoon at the new Highmark Stadium, Josh Allen led the Buffalo Bills on a pair of scoring drives as the Bills kicked off the preseason with a 29-14 win over the Carolina Panthers in the first game ever played in Buffalo’s new palace. Observations and standouts from Buffalo’s 29-14 win over Carolina Bills fans have heard all offseason about how quarterback Josh Allen and new wide receiver D.J. Moore have been working on their chemistry, and on Saturday, in the team’s preseason debut, that on-field-rapport and big-play potential was on display for all to see as Allen connected with Moore for three catches for 61 yards, including a 32-yard gain on a short crossing route the very first time Allen targeted Moore. title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: wide receiver Khalil Shakir
summary: The Buffalo Bills had a wide receiver problem last season. In short, they didn’t have a player who profiles as a true “alpha” in the receiver room. Sure, they had some good players, but most football people viewed those players as good pieces, not true game-wreckers who can thrive regardless of the situation or defense […]
full_text: Bills receiver Khalil Shakir looks for extra yards after a catch. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Buffalo Bills had a wide receiver problem last season. In short, they didn’t have a player who profiles as a true “alpha” in the receiver room. Sure, they had some good players, but most football people viewed those players as good pieces, not true game-wreckers who can thrive regardless of the situation or defense they face. Is that underselling Buffalo’s top wideout for the last two seasons? Perhaps it is; however, just from a statistical standpoint, that “top” wideout wouldn’t have been the top guy in nearly every other top-flight passing offense in the NFL. What he was asked to do in terms of his route tree also seemed to be a limiting factor. Was that a design flaw, or a product of having a rough supporting cast? In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss the man who has been Buffalo’s top wideout over the last two seasons. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: Khalil Shakir Number: 10 Position: WR Height/Weight: 6’ 190 lbs. Age: 26 (27 on 2/3/2027) Experience/Draft: 5; selected by Buffalo in the fifth round (No. 148 overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft College: Boise State Acquired: Fifth-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): This season marks the first year of Shakir’s four-year, $52.866 million extension that he signed in February 2025. His cap hit for this season is $6.792 million. If Buffalo releases him, they’ll carry a dead cap charge of $25.796 million. 2025 Recap: Shakir once again slotted in—literally and figuratively—as Buffalo’s top wideout, and he once again led the team in nearly every receiving category. He played in one more game last season than he did in 2024 despite suffering a high ankle sprain in Buffalo’s Return of the Blue and Red scrimmage. In fact, Shakir missed no game time due to that sprain, as he returned to practice ahead of Buffalo’s Week One win over the Baltimore Ravens and played in that game. The only game he missed was the regular-season finale, and he sat alongside multiple other starters as Buffalo rested ahead of their Wild Card date with the Jacksonville Jaguars. Shakir led the team in targets (95), receptions (72), and receiving yards (719). Dalton Kincaid led the team with five receiving touchdowns, but Shakir was second with four. In the playoffs, Shakir was once again quarterback Josh Allen’s go-to guy, leading the team by a wide margin in targets (21), receptions (19), and receiving yards (157). Shakir also was used as a punt returner at multiple points throughout the season. In the regular season, Shakir returned 16 punts and averaged 7.8 yards per return. Both totals led the Bills. He did not return a punt in the postseason, but he was back there to do so a few times; he fair caught a punt in Buffalo’s 33-30 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos in the Divisional Round of the playoffs. Throughout the season, Shakir was used mainly at or near the line of scrimmage , as his average depth of target was the lowest among all wideouts who saw at least 50 targets last year. Shakir averaged just 3.8 yards per target. Positional outlook: Shakir is one of fourteen wideouts on the current roster. Mac Dalena, Ja’Mori Maclin, Max Tomczak, Stephen Gosnell, Mecole Hardman Jr., Trent Sherfield, Joshua Palmer, Keon Coleman, Skyler Bell, DJ Moore, Tyrell Shavers, Quentin Skinner, and Dante Pettis are the others. 2026 Offseason: Shakir is healthy, and he’s already looking like he might have a different, more diverse role this season. He’s been used much more downfield in practices so far. 2026 Season outlook: Maybe I’m crazy, but I think that the addition of DJ Moore will actually help Shakir’s production this season, not harm it. Sure, he might not see 100 targets—especially if tight end Dalton Kincaid can actually stay healthy—but Shakir will likely see more passes in downfield areas. Yes, he’s excellent at handling screen passes and turning them into long gains, but he’s also an adept route runner who has plenty of untapped downfield upside. In a more diverse role, he could come closer to his 2023 production where he averaged 16.8 yards per reception. Not coincidentally, that was the last season that the Bills had a true alpha in the receivier room in Stefon Diggs. Shakir is a phenomenal wideout, and if he fills the proper role, he could help any offense be better. He’s been miscast over the last two seasons as the top dog in Buffalo’s passing attack. Adding Moore will help him to improve, and if the Bills can also limit his use on punt returns by deploying someone they can trust to handle the gig, it will also help keep Shakir out of harm’s way with more unnecessary snaps. Again, Shakir is a good punt returner, and if he did it more consistently, I think he might even be able to be great at it. However, I don’t think it’s a good use of resources for the Bills to have their WR2 exposing himself to more hits on special teams if they can avoid it. Look for Shakir to continue doing plenty of damage on short passes and screens this season, but don’t be surprised when he sees more downfield targets, either. He’s a legitimate threat at all three levels of the defense, and I’m excited to see his next level unlocked.

title: An under-the-radar memorable moment from the Buffalo Bills win over the Carolina Panthers
summary: Like many fans of the Buffalo Bills, I try not to overreact when it comes to the team’s performance during the preseason. I have a hard time remembering anything from previous preseason games outside of Christian Wade, AJ McCarron, and a friend of mine melting down on Facebook about Case Keenum’s performance in the 2022. […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - JANUARY 11: Frank Gore Jr. #20 of the Buffalo Bills warms up prior to an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Buffalo Bills at EverBank Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Jacksonville, FL. (Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images) | Getty Images Like many fans of the Buffalo Bills, I try not to overreact when it comes to the team’s performance during the preseason. I have a hard time remembering anything from previous preseason games outside of Christian Wade, AJ McCarron, and a friend of mine melting down on Facebook about Case Keenum’s performance in the 2022. But on Saturday’s game there was a special moment that I will remember choose to remember for all of the right reasons. Late in the fourth quarter on Saturday, Frank Gore Jr. followed his offensive linemen into the end zone for a touchdown, extending the Bills lead to 28-7. Rather than celebrate himself, Gore found offensive lineman Bruno Fina and handed him the football. Fina spiked the football and the offense celebrated emphatically together. If you have not put 2-and-2 together yet, both Gore and Fina have fathers that played for the Bills. I was actually able to catch up with Bruno Fina prior to the start of camp with Joe Miller from Overreaction Buffalo during last month’s Mafia-Con event. For Gore it was just one season with the Bills in 2019, where he helped the Bills reach the playoffs while rushing for 599 yards. Fina spent 10 of his 11 NFL seasons in Buffalo, starting 131 games after being selected in the first round out of Arizona. The former first rounder also appeared in two Super Bowls while playing for the Bills during the 19912 and 1993 seasons. I can understand that a moment like this may go unnoticed by many fans on Saturday, but for me I am going to remember it as one of the more memorable moments in all of my years watching Bills preseason football.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 28 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 17: Trai Turner #70 of the Carolina Panthers during the second half during their game against the Atlanta Falcons at Bank of America Stadium on November 17, 2019 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #28. Trai Turner One of the best things you can have as a football team is a stalwart offensive lineman that is very good for his position and generally stays healthy. The Carolina Panthers had that in the mid to late 2010s with Trai Turner at right guard. Turner had a rapid ascent from 3 star recruit coming out of high school to NFL Draft prospect after his redshirt sophomore year at LSU. The Panthers selected Turner in the third round of the 2014 NFL Draft, and it didn’t take long for him to make that look like an incredible decision. He earned the starting right guard spot during his rookie season, and he would not relinquish that spot for the entirety of his career in Carolina. Turner would establish himself as one of the league’s best interior linemen during that rookie season. He played five more years in Carolina, never missing more than three games and making the Pro Bowl every single season. He was elite both as a pass protector and a run blocker and helped some offenses with Cam Newton and underwhelming skill position support find their way to success. Despite the accolades, the Panthers traded the then 26 year old Turner for 31 year old offensive tackle Russell Okung, presumably to get out from under the massive (for a guard at the time) contract that Turner had recently been given by since departed GM Dave Gettleman. It proved to be a prescient move. Turner played just nine games for the Chargers before getting released after one season. He spent one season each with the Steelers and Commanders after that before a torn quad in camp with the Saints effectively ended his career. Turner was never the best guard in the NFL, but he was always near the top of the list and was a household name in some respects, which isn’t common for a guard. He was a steady presence on the offensive line for several years, and that hasn’t been a common occurrence for the Panthers throughout their history. For that, he lands at number 28 on the list of top 100 Panthers of all time.

title: Xavier Woods Injury, When It May Have Occurred
summary: The Chicago Bears suffered some more bad luck to the defensive back department on Saturday when new safety Xavier Woods sustained what we know to be a groin injury. Woods was signed by the Bears on August 7 following a significant injury to Coby Bryant, who is slated to miss 4-6 months. Woods has started […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears safety Xavier Woods (23) during the first half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Mike Dinovo-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears suffered some more bad luck to the defensive back department on Saturday when new safety Xavier Woods sustained what we know to be a groin injury. Woods was signed by the Bears on August 7 following a significant injury to Coby Bryant, who is slated to miss 4-6 months. Woods has started 121 games in the NFL, and he played under current Bears’ DB coach Al Harris while he was with Dallas in 2020. At this point, it is unknown how long Woods will be out and how severe the injury is. Head coach Ben Johnson commented on the injury following the Bears’ preseason win over Cleveland, but that’s all that we have heard so far. I went back and dissected the tape on Sunday morning to see if I could find any clues as to where the injury occurred, as well as to get an idea of how severe it could be. I should point out, of course, that I am not a medical professional. Sometimes injuries like this are tricky and are more severe than they appear, but I’d like to share with you what I observed. Woods only played 9 snaps on defense on Saturday, all in the first quarter. I watched all of them as closely as possible, and it was hard to decipher when the injury occurred as nothing really stood out. Woods never reacts like someone who was injured, nor does he appear to suffer when it comes to his mobility on the field. The closest thing I could find to a possible injury happened on Woods’ third-to-last play in the game. Woods tracked down Browns RB Dylan Sampson on a 43 yard HB screen. Woods showed off his speed and range, coming all the way across the field to make the stop. At the very end of the clip that I cut below, you will notice Woods briefly point at someone down the sideline. At first, I thought he might be pointing at a teammate on the field, but after viewing the play from a different angle, that doesn’t appear to be the case. Not seeing much on film w/ the Xavier Woods injury. 3 plays before he left the game, he chased down Dylan Sampson on a screen. He appeared to briefly motion down the #Bears sideline after the play, but he stayed in on the next 2 plays and appeared to be moving fine. #DaBears pic.twitter.com/JzjLrD6scS — Ryan Droste (@ryandroste) August 16, 2026 It’s possible he tweaked something here and was alerting his coaches or medical staff, but that’s merely speculation on my part. You be the judge. What I can tell you is that Woods did not come out of the game after this. On the next play, Woods was in coverage jogging around the field and appeared to be fine. On the last play that he was in the game, Woods pursued Browns’ RB Ahmani Marshall and looks to be moving fine again, even cutting directions on the play. He hops up at the end of the play and doesn’t react like someone who is severely hurt. The next play, he was in coverage and jogging around the field. This was his final play in the game. He's in pursuit and changes direction. He didn't ask to come out of the game after the play but noticed a sub come in and then jogged off. The game broadcast showed him up… pic.twitter.com/bKYJo8SSsq — Ryan Droste (@ryandroste) August 16, 2026 It was after this play that Woods was taken out of the game and he never returned. As you will see from the footage below, he does not motion to be taken out of the game. Instead, he noticed the substitution being made and jogs off the field. They even zoom on him on the sideline. This is from the game broadcast when he leaves the game. Injuries are weird and you never know for sure, but hopefully it's nothing major. The #Bears certainly need him in that secondary. pic.twitter.com/sHB68gTjkM — Ryan Droste (@ryandroste) August 16, 2026 Again, Woods does not seem to be severely injured (visually at least). Perhaps this is wishful thinking. The Bears very much need the experience that he brings to the table in starting opposite of rookie Dillon Thieneman while Bryant is out. Another long-term injury to the backend of this defense would be devastating. We’ll have to wait for another update on the severity of the injury. I’m just pointing out to our readers what I observed above. I remain hopeful that this will not be a long-term injury, but we’ll find out for sure in due time. Sometimes even minor groin injuries can linger for a longer period of time that originally expected.

title: Bears activate left tackle Ozzy Trapilo from PUP list
summary: The Chicago Bears activated left tackle Ozzy Trapilo from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list on Sunday. As a result of the activation, he is now able to participate in practices and preseason games. Trapilo ruptured his patellar tendon in the Bears’ Wild Card win over the Packers in January. For much of the […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Ozzy Trapilo #75 of the Chicago Bears defends during an NFL wild card playoff game against the Green Bay Packers at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Chicago Bears activated left tackle Ozzy Trapilo from the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) list on Sunday. As a result of the activation, he is now able to participate in practices and preseason games. Trapilo ruptured his patellar tendon in the Bears’ Wild Card win over the Packers in January. For much of the 2026 offseason, the anticipation was that the 24-year-old would miss most, if not all of the 2026-27 NFL season. However, it appears he’s now healthy enough to be activated, which figures to make him ready for Week 1 of the Bears’ upcoming season. Now that Trapilo has been activated from the PUP list, he cannot be placed back on the list. If he happens to suffer another major injury this season, his future injury designation would have to be the injured reserve. A second-round pick out of Boston College in 2025, Trapilo made the switch from right tackle to left tackle leading up to his rookie year. He started at left tackle for the Eagles in 2022, but he spent each of his final two seasons at right tackle. Considering he had to switch sides and adjust to the NFL level of speed and physicality, he performed quite admirably. Trapilo’s 73.3 PFN OL Impact Score ranked No. 66 among all qualified NFL offensive tackles. The eighth offensive tackle off the board in the 2025 NFL Draft, he graded fifth among all rookie tackles last season. He graded better than players selected ahead of him like Josh Simmons, Aireontae Ersery, and Josh Conerly Jr. Should Trapilo be ready for Week 1, it’s reasonable to assume he’ll start at left tackle for the Bears, as he did to finish up last season. Braxton Jones has taken a majority of starting reps at left tackle in his absence, with the likes of Jedrick Wills Jr. and Kiran Amegadjie also seeing reps there. The Bears also announced that defensive backs K.C. Eziomume and Gervarrius Owens, and wide receiver Kyron Hudson were waived with an injury settlement.

summary: The Chicago Bears and Cleveland Browns took two different approaches to this game. The Bears sat many of their starters, including quarterback Caleb Williams, while the Browns trotted out most of their ones to start the game and played QB Deshaun Watson the entire first half. The Bears’ first-string offense did get in some work, […]
full_text: Aug 15, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Chicago Bears defensive end Jamree Kromah (59) sacks Cleveland Browns quarterback Dillon Gabriel (6) during the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Chicago Bears and Cleveland Browns took two different approaches to this game. The Bears sat many of their starters, including quarterback Caleb Williams, while the Browns trotted out most of their ones to start the game and played QB Deshaun Watson the entire first half. The Bears’ first-string offense did get in some work, though, as head coach Ben Johnson said they got in a “phenomenal throwing session” and ran over 60 plays. He added he’s not sure if they’ll play the starters in the next preseason game, and that he’s “happy with what the offense looks like right now.” But back to yesterday’s game. The Bears put up 34 unanswered points after falling behind 10-0, and they coasted to a 34-10 win. Ben Johnson’s Bears have yet to lose a preseason game. Chicago had more total yards (430 to 314) and more first downs (22 to 13), but the Browns had the time-of-possession edge (34:03 to 25:57). The Browns also had more penalties, with 5 for 42 yards to just 2 for 10 for the Bears, something Johnson discussed in his opening remarks at his postgame presser. “Proud of our guys and how they played,” he said. “We talked about being disciplined in all three phases, and we really saw it today. I think two penalties on the day from all three phases. We haven’t had a practice yet where we’ve had that few fouls. So that was really encouraging to see.” Before we get into some more numbers, here are all the Bears who did not play against the Browns. And here is how the Bears started the day on both sides of the ball. Here are the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats. Offense With so many players participating for the Bears in the preseason, I’ll split the snap count lists into two for both the offense and the defense. Also, keep in mind that special teams snaps in these preseason games often indicate the reserve players coaches have in mind for the third phase, either on the 53-man roster or for the practice squad. Tyson Bagent got the start and was 13 of 22 (59.1%), for 169 passing yards, with 1 touchdown, 1 interception, and a 79.5 passer rating. Kaden Davis led the Bears in receiving with 4 receptions for 88 yards. Roschon Johnson led the Bears in rushing with 8 attempts for 34 yards. He added a 3-yard catch. QB3 Case Keenum came in and went 9 of 10 for 151 yards, with 2 TDs and a perfect 158.3 passer rating. Running back Salvon Ahmed had 72 yards from scrimmage, including a 49-yard touchdown off a screen from Keenum. Salvon Ahmed takes the screen 49 yards for a TD 😤 CLEvsCHI on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/O8AlWhLUED — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Be sure you take a moment to appreciate the blocking on that play above. Wideout Maurice Alexander had 3 grabs for 42 yards and a TD. Running back Brittain Brown rushed 5 times for 8 yards and had 2 receptions for 12 yards and a TD. UDFA running back Coleman Bennett had 4 runs for 19 yards and a TD. Qadry Ismail (1 catch, 8 yards), who is listed as a WR above, is actually a tight end, so did you notice the starting lineup the Bears opened up with was 14 personnel (1 RB/4 tight ends)? Defense Defensive end Jamree Kromah, who spent part of 2024 and all of 2o25 on the Bears practice squad, had a huge day with 6 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, 2 sacks, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery. Head coach Ben Johnson said that Kromah had a nice springtime taking to the coaching and new techniques, and was flashing then, but wondered, “Is this the time he’s going to turn it on? And you don’t know.” “And then you go into a game like this, and you see the get off, you see the relentlessness,” Johnson said about Kromah. “I mean, you could feel his presence every single snap, and I’m standing close to the d-lineman, and they’re just hooting and hollering and cheering for him because they’re as excited as he is cuz they’re seeing him going out there making plays and making an impact like that. He’s such a hard worker. I know he’s been in the program now for a minute, and to see him have some success on the field like that, that was huge.” “One thing I did for sure was I changed my body, changed my nutrition, because I was much heavier last year,” Kromah said via chicagobears.com . “So I wanted to make some changes by losing weight. I lost over 20 pounds, but got stronger and then put more lean mass on. So this is the best I have felt … I had to look at the man in the mirror and be true to myself, and come up with a real plan.” Linebacker Ruben Hyppolite II, who left the game with a shoulder injury, led the Bears with 7 tackles, while adding a TFL and a pass defended. Defensive tackle Neville Gallimore had 3 tackles and 2 TFLs. Defensive lineman James Lynch got reps at both end and tackle, and while he had a sack negated by a penalty, he had 2 tackles, a QB hit, and a PD. Rookie corner Malik Muhammad II got the start at nickel and had 5 tackles. Cornerback Beanie Bishop Jr. had 2 interceptions, 3 PD, and 2 tackles. Defensive end Jeremiah Martin had 2 tackles, a TFL, and a sack on a nice zone blitz where the Bears sent two defensive backs off either side while dropping both defensive tackles into coverage, Special Teams *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos was 2 for 3 on field goals with a long of 51, and was 4 for 4 on extra points. Tory Taylor had 4 punts and a 47.0 average (32.3 net), with 1 punt inside the twenty. Receiver Kaden Davis had a 23-yard punt return. Corner Dontae Manning had 3 special teams tackles. Wideout Jahdae Walker and tight end Hayden Large each had 2 special teams tackles. title: Jack Endries gets off to a good start in NFL debut
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals may have found something at the bottom of the 2026 NFL Draft. Rookie tight end Jack Endries made his presence felt Thursday night in Cincinnati’s 16-14 preseason victory over the Detroit Lions, finishing with three receptions for 25 yards and catching the Bengals’ only touchdown. And his first NFL touchdown came from […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals may have found something at the bottom of the 2026 NFL Draft. Rookie tight end Jack Endries made his presence felt Thursday night in Cincinnati’s 16-14 preseason victory over the Detroit Lions, finishing with three receptions for 25 yards and catching the Bengals’ only touchdown. And his first NFL touchdown came from a quarterback who has been playing professional football almost as long as Endries has been alive. Joe Flacco found Endries for a four-yard touchdown, giving the rookie a moment he won’t soon forget. “Awesome person to catch a touchdown from,” Endries said after the game. “That guy’s a legend. I play catch with him every day, so it’s cool. Got a little connection there.” "Awesome person to catch a TD from." "That guy's a legend." Postgame with Jack Endries on catching his first TD from Joe Flacco. Flacco also made sure he saved the ball for him. #Bengals @FOX19 pic.twitter.com/1rGpkB5Fgt — Jeremy Rauch (@FOX19Jeremy) August 14, 2026 Flacco apparently understood what the moment meant to the 22-year-old. After the play, the veteran quarterback made sure the football didn’t disappear. “I heard he ran after the play and grabbed the ball,” Endries said. “I didn’t know that. That’s really cool.” For Endries, Thursday night’s performance was the latest step in a journey that began with considerably less fanfare. Endries originally walked on at Cal, redshirting in 2022 before developing into one of the most productive pass-catching tight ends in college football. He caught 35 passes for 407 yards and two touchdowns in 2023, earning Freshman All-America recognition. The following season, he broke out with 56 receptions for 623 yards and two touchdowns, earning honorable mention All-ACC honors. His quarterback at Cal was Fernando Mendoza, who went on to become the No. 1 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft. Endries transferred to Texas for the 2025 season and started all 13 games for the Longhorns, catching 33 passes for 346 yards and three touchdowns. He finished his college career with 124 receptions for 1,376 yards and seven touchdowns in 39 games while starting every one of them. Despite that production, Endries waited much longer than expected to hear his name called on draft weekend. The Bengals finally selected him in the seventh round with the 221st overall pick. Endries came into camp with something to prove, and he still has a long way to go. He seems to understand that catching passes, even touchdown passes, won’t be enough to get him there. “A tight end is a do-it-all type of guy that can play special teams and play every position on offense,” Endries said Thursday night. Endries still has plenty of work ahead of him before the Bengals make their final roster decisions. One preseason game isn’t going to settle that competition. But Thursday night’s efforts were a pretty good way for a seventh-round rookie to introduce himself.

The attorney for Daniels released a statement to LSU that it can no longer use his name, image, and likeness, according to a letter sent to Tigers athletic director Verge Ausberry. “The Daniels family is deeply disappointed and feels profoundly disrespected by LSU’s decision to give Jayden’s number to another player,” the statement from Daniels’ spokesperson said. “Jayden and his family had every reason to believe that his number would remain a meaningful part of his LSU legacy and would be honored and protected in recognition of his extraordinary contributions to the university.” Sophomore cornerback DJ Pickett is officially rocking number 5 this season, and this is the first time an LSU player has worn that jersey number since the Commanders drafted Daniels. Daniels’ representative feels he is being treated differently than Joe Burrow because no one has worn number 9 since Burrow finished his career with LSU. Burrow was asked after the preseason game what his thoughts were on the situation, and his response was quite simple: “I don’t know too much about it. I just heard about it a couple of hours ago. I don’t necessarily have too many thoughts at this time. I just…I don’t know enough about the situation to have any thoughts, I would say.” The Bengals franchise QB was also asked about his number not being used by LSU since leaving, and he stated that they told him they wouldn’t use it again. “They told me that they wouldn’t use it again. But you never know what happens,” he said. Daniels also released a statement regarding the controversy, so it will be interesting to see how this all plays out.

title: National reporter goes to bat for DJ Turner
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have been trying to draft a defensive star for a long time, with the last one being Jessie Bates, their second-round pick from the 2018 Draft. Now, it seems they may have done it with their second-round pick from 2023, cornerback DJ Turner from Michigan, who took a step toward elite play in 2025. […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have been trying to draft a defensive star for a long time, with the last one being Jessie Bates, their second-round pick from the 2018 Draft. Now, it seems they may have done it with their second-round pick from 2023, cornerback DJ Turner from Michigan, who took a step toward elite play in 2025. It seems the Bengals and their fans aren’t the only ones recognizing Turner’s growth and potential. In a recent tweet , Dan Hoard shares a quote from ESPN reporter Ben Solak on Turner’s talent and how he will try to get him attention. “I will single-handedly get DJ Turner national attention — I swear to God I will,” said Solak. “Every time I’ve turned on Bengals’ defensive film the last couple of years, you just see a guy who moves as the top corners move and who can see the ball the way the top corners can.” It is nice to see a Bengals player getting attention from a national reporter, and if the Bengals are going to rebound defensively from the last few years, a key will be Turner’s continued growth. With a better pass rush, especially from the Bengals’ much-improved defensive tackle position, Turner may not have to hold up in coverage for as long, or may have fewer errant throws to defend. While it is nice to see a Bengals player receive praise, it is concerning that the second-round pick is entering the final year of his rookie contract without a deal. It is reminiscent of the last great defensive player the Bengals drafted in Jessie Bates. They ultimately let him walk after he played on the franchise tag for a year. After joining the Falcons, Bates continued his great play, earning two more Second-Team All-Pro selections. The Bengals need to be sure the same thing doesn’t happen with Turner, and ideally lock him down before another hopefully great season that would skyrocket his price even more.

What started with a visit from former DE Jadeveon Clowney , only to be spurned as the former top overall pick returned to the Houston Texans, continued with a workout with DE Tyus Bowser , who hasn’t played a full season since 2021 and was out all of last year, and then a visit from former Browns DE Za’Darius Smith might have found the finish line. Emphasis, at least for now, on “might.” Following Cleveland’s opening preseason loss to the Chicago Bears, where the pass rush was inconsistent to non-existent, Mary Kay Cabot is reporting that Smith is likely to return to the Browns: #Browns are expected to re-sign edge rusher Za'Darius Smith as early as today; DT Mike Hall Jr. is on the mend and more: —> https://t.co/66NPXtStqd — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) August 16, 2026 Cabot, the long-time beat reporter, saw her report aggregated (as we are doing here) across a number of platforms, including Instagram . For a short time before it was deleted, Smith seemed to express confusion about Cabot’s report in a reply to the IG post, stating he had not signed and has a workout coming up on Monday with another team. That comment has since been deleted, but there has been no more reporting on Smith’s plans since Cabot’s initial report. Cabot noted in the report how Smith would fit : In the Browns’ attack-minded defense, Smith would have a chance to get back into the eight or nine sack range, and would be a tremendous help to Verse, who’s eager to learn from top veteran edge rushers. A two-time Pro Bowler, Verse is only in his third season and has relied primarily on his power and explosiveness off the ball. But he’s hoping to add to his pass-rush repertoire, and Smith would be just the man for the job. Smith surprisingly retired last year while a part of the Philadelphia Eagles. The Browns traded for Smith in May of 2023. During his time in Cleveland, Smith had 10.5 sacks, 50 tackles, and 27 quarterback hits. The Browns traded Smith and a 2026 seventh-round draft pick to the Lions in exchange for a 2025 fifth-round pick and a 2026 sixth-round pick at the trade deadline in 2024. In his 11 years in the NFL, Smith compiled 343 tackles, 176 QB hits, 87 tackles for loss, and 70.5 sacks. We will continue to cover Smith’s free agency and see if the reunion in Berea, Ohio becomes official. title: 3 reasons why Von Miller signing is awesome for Cowboys
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are signing Von Miller. That is a real sentence, people. Whatever you think of Von these days it feels fair to say that you can at least agree that this is an exciting thing. The Cowboys are very much awake and alert, and Von’s presence is the latest proof of that. Miller […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 21: Von Miller #24 of the Washington Commanders celebrates a sack against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half of the NFL 2025 game at Northwest Stadium on September 21, 2025 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Jess Rapfogel/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are signing Von Miller. That is a real sentence, people. Whatever you think of Von these days it feels fair to say that you can at least agree that this is an exciting thing. The Cowboys are very much awake and alert, and Von’s presence is the latest proof of that. Miller is one of the most decorated players of his generation and has two Super Bowls to his name, not to mention Super Bowl 50 MVP honors, to prove it. He can significantly help the Cowboys in a number of ways which is why the move is so exciting. Here are 3 reasons that are specifically interesting in the exciting department. Von has been there and done that The Cowboys have spent all of this season (since training camp began) talking about how they are proud to have Super Bowl aspirations. Simply put, they are confident in themselves and good for them that they are. Through all of the franchise’s recent missteps and misgivings they have not really had someone around who has climbed to the top of the NFL’s mountain. Dallas has failed, we all can admit this, and they have failed as a group of equal novices. No one was around to keep things in check when the going got tough. My point isn’t that Von Miller can singlehandedly save the day if times get tough in a playoff game, but he knows how treacherous those roads can be. That wisdom is invaluable to a team who isn’t being shy about going where he has been. Von doesn’t have to be VON MILLER here It goes without saying that Von Miller is not the player that he once was. Okay. So? The Cowboys have Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku to manage their pass rushing needs from a priority standpoint. When they are subbed out Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark will help make life as easy as they can for the reserve players, and it is at this point in time that the mercenary known as Von Miller can strike. We saw Jadeveon Clowney sort of take advantage of this role last year, and that was on a team that was very much up a creek in terms of the total defensive effort. Von simply has to help raise the ceiling for the Cowboys. He can chase that with this team. The foundational elements are taking care of the floor. This will help the young players significantly The Cowboys signed Von Miller just one day after Malachi Lawrence did not set the world on fire in his NFL debut. If you were expecting Malachi to do anything special then maybe you need to reassess what’s fair from an expectation standpoint. But now Malachi gets to learn from Von Miller. So does Donovan Ezeiruaku, and so does James Houston. Heck, so does Rashan Gary. Von is a rising tide that is going to lift all boats and provide an important mentor for the pass rushers in the way that Jason Peters did on the other side of the trenches back in Tyler Smith’s rookie season. It isn’t every day that a future Hall of Famer joins the group and offers his services both on the field and in the classroom. The Cowboys now have that in Von Miller.

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 28
summary: It is Day 28 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PA - NOVEMBER 13: Ezekiel Elliott #21 of the Dallas Cowboys celebrates his 32-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter during the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Heinz Field on November 13, 2016 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images It is Day 28 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. It’s Day 28 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the defining victories of the Dak Prescott and Ezekiel Elliott era. In a game filled with momentum swings, clutch plays and late drama, the Cowboys went into one of the NFL’s toughest environments and outlasted the Steelers. Sunday, November 13, 2016 Heinz Field, Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 35, Pittsburgh Steelers 30 Dallas entered the matchup riding a seven-game winning streak, but many questioned whether the rookie-led offense could handle a road game against Ben Roethlisberger, Antonio Brown and Le’Veon Bell. Those doubts quickly disappeared. Prescott played with remarkable poise, while Elliott consistently found room behind one of the league’s best offensive lines. The game remained close throughout the afternoon. Dallas built an early lead before Pittsburgh answered with a series of big plays. Brown made several spectacular catches, Bell found success both as a runner and receiver, and Roethlisberger threw for over 400 yards to keep the Steelers within striking distance. Every time Pittsburgh threatened to take control, Prescott had an answer. He threw touchdown passes to Dez Bryant and Jason Witten while extending drives with timely scrambles. Elliott added two rushing touchdowns, and the Cowboys continued to answer every Steelers score in what quickly became one of the NFL’s best games of the season. The drama reached another level in the final two minutes. Roethlisberger connected with Brown for a 15-yard touchdown with just 42 seconds remaining, giving Pittsburgh a 30-29 lead. Heinz Field erupted, and it appeared Dallas’ winning streak was about to come to an end. Prescott calmly took over. On the very next drive, he found Witten for a huge gain before Elliott burst through the middle, made one decisive cut and raced 32 yards for the game-winning touchdown with only nine seconds remaining. The rookie running back crossed the goal line untouched, silencing the Pittsburgh crowd and completing one of the most memorable finishes of the decade. Prescott finished with 319 passing yards, two touchdowns and added a rushing score, continuing one of the greatest rookie quarterback seasons in NFL history. Elliott rushed for 114 yards and two touchdowns, including the unforgettable game winner, while Bryant caught six passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. This game belongs on the countdown because it perfectly captured what made the 2016 Cowboys special. Prescott never looked rattled in a hostile environment, Elliott consistently delivered in the biggest moments and Dallas repeatedly answered every challenge. Against one of the AFC’s elite teams, the Cowboys showed they could win a heavyweight fight, and the victory became the defining moment of their 13-3 season. #Cowboys vs #Steelers 2016 Week 10 Final Score: Dallas Cowboys 35, Pittsburgh Steelers 30 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/GeSqBnkWNI — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 16, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game This remains one of a limited number of NFL games where both teams scored go-ahead touchdowns in the final minute, with Dallas ultimately having the last answer. summary: One of the unique things about yesterday’s game against the Seahawks is that both teams rested most of their presumptive starters. The Cowboys gave three of their presumptive starters (Shavon Revel, P.J. Locke, Caleb Downs) and two core backups (T.J. Bass and Luke Schoonmaker) only a little more than a handful of snaps before their […]

The Cowboys gave three of their presumptive starters (Shavon Revel, P.J. Locke, Caleb Downs) and two core backups (T.J. Bass and Luke Schoonmaker) only a little more than a handful of snaps before their day ended early. And that gives us ample room to review the snap counts from Sunday’s game to get a better feel for what is happening to the depth across the roster. One of the quirks of only starting backups is that somebody still has to start , which effectively already establishes two tiers among the backups: Starters and subs, or second-team and third-team players. The first thing to look at is a simple snap count which details which player was in on how many plays. Curtis Robinson led the team with eight tackles, James Houston and Isaiah Land had a sack each, while Trikweze Bridges and Tyrus Wheat shared a sack. Who do you think should move up into the green tier next week against the 49ers, a game in which the Cowboys will again rest their starters? Special teams is often the deciding factor for the bottom-of-the-guys to make the final 53. body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table { border: 1px solid #000 !important; border-collapse: collapse !important; } body .sbnu-legacy-content-table td, body .sbnu-legacy-content-table th { padding: 0px 6px !important; } Special Teams snap counts Player POS ST snaps J.Wood S 8 DJ.Rogers TE 7 C.Robinson LB 7 T.Wheat OLB 7 I.Land OLB 7 M.Trigg TE 6 C.Brown WR 6 J.Barron LB 6 C.Carson CB 6 A.Clark S 6 L.Patterson LB 6 It’s probably too early to deduce anything from these numbers, but we’ll watch them closely as preseason progresses. Another thing that has to be mentioned in the context of special teams is the “hidden yardage” in this game. Bill Parcells used to say that a 100-yard advantage in field position, or “hidden yardage,” was worth seven points (others may use the same formula, he’s just the one I associate this with). Here’s a look at the hidden yardage differential in Sunday’s game: Dallas: 134 yards (sum of starting field positions on all drives) Seattle: 334 yards This is in part the result of the muffed by Traeshon Holden and two good punt returns versus zero for the Cowboys. The Cowboys were lucky to have the defense bail them out on not one but three (!!) red-zone drives by the Seahawks. The hidden yardage advantage alone should have been worth 14 points for the Seahawks, according to Parcells, so special teams should get some very special attention in practice going forward. An finally, Curtis Robinson is this week’s ironman, having played a total of 53 snaps, 46 on defense and seven on special teams.

Hopefully a sign of things to come. Results of preseason games are not the most important thing in the world. What matters is how the players play so that the overall roster can be put together in the best way possible. Something we do every week here at Blogging The Boys is a stock report following games, and an argument exists that these are most critical around the preseason for this very reason. Let’s begin. Stock Up: Jaydon Blue This definitely felt bigger in the moment, but even after some time to marinate on things it feels right.
