title: Aaron Donald completes 2nd official Rams workout
summary: Aaron Donald had his second official workout with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, adding another chapter to what has become one of the biggest NFL storylines of the summer. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the latest development via the league’s transaction wire, providing another indication that Donald is seriously considering a return to the team […]
full_text: Aaron Donald had his second official workout with the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, adding another chapter to what has become one of the biggest NFL storylines of the summer. ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the latest development via the league’s transaction wire, providing another indication that Donald is seriously considering a return to the team where he built a Hall of Fame career. The Aaron Donald comeback saga continues to provide more and more smoke. For the second time this summer, Aaron Donald was listed today as working out for the Rams on the NFL’s transaction wire. pic.twitter.com/d11nkFZugX — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 16, 2026 Donald’s first official workout with the Rams came earlier this month after the three-time Defensive Player of the Year returned to the team’s facility. That workout was significant enough that the Rams were required to report his participation to the NFL because he was using team equipment. Now, a second official workout has been reported by Los Angeles. The Rams have already assembled a potentially dominant defense, highlighted by the blockbuster addition of Myles Garrett. Adding Donald to a defensive line featuring Garrett, Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, and the rest of Los Angeles’ talented front could completely change the ceiling of the unit. Donald retired after the 2023 season with 111 career sacks and eight first-team All-Pro selections, leaving little doubt about what he accomplished during his decade with the Rams. And the clock is beginning to tick. There are now 25 days until the Rams open the regular season against the San Francisco 49ers on September 10 in Melbourne, Australia. The Week 1 matchup is scheduled for the Melbourne Cricket Ground and will be the Rams’ first regular-season game of the 2026 season. Despite that approaching deadline, head coach Sean McVay isn’t putting one on Donald. McVay recently said he does not want to put an “invisible deadline” on Donald’s decision. While the Rams would obviously love to know whether their franchise legend plans to return, McVay has emphasized that Donald needs the space to make the decision on his own timeline. McVay did add that he hopes a decision comes “sooner than later”. That patience could ultimately be important. Donald has already accomplished virtually everything a player can accomplish, so this decision is about more than football. He has to determine whether he wants to put his body through another NFL season and whether another Super Bowl pursuit is worth coming out of retirement. But completing a second official workout is certainly noteworthy. For now, Donald hasn’t officially announced that he is returning. Yet with 25 days remaining before the Rams face the 49ers, the possibility of seeing No. 99 back in Los Angeles is becoming harder to ignore.
author: Steven Ridings

title: Rams make surprising addition to roster on Sunday
summary: The Los Angeles Rams signed punter Jack Bouwmeester on Sunday, giving them two on the 90-man roster headed into their second preseason game against the New Orleans Saints this week. Bouwmeester is Australian and qualifies for the league’s international pathway program exemption, meaning that the Rams can control his rights without him counting against their […]
full_text: DALLAS, TX - OCTOBER 11: Punter Jack Bouwmeester #19 of the Texas Longhorns holds the Golden Hat while surrounded by fans after winning the Allstate Red River Rivalry between Oklahoma and Texas on October 11, 2025, at Cotton Bowl Stadium in Dallas, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams signed punter Jack Bouwmeester on Sunday, giving them two on the 90-man roster headed into their second preseason game against the New Orleans Saints this week. Bouwmeester is Australian and qualifies for the league’s international pathway program exemption, meaning that the Rams can control his rights without him counting against their practice squad limits. Ethan Evans continues to be one of the best punters in the NFL, so this signing would seemingly not be a threat to his job. The Rams signed former 49ers punter Jack Bouwmeester as their international exemption (doesn't count vs roster limit). I am sure the NFL is happy that the Aussie therefore remains on track to be in Melbourne for Week 1 — David Lombardi (@LombardiHimself) August 16, 2026 Bouwmeester, 27, played college football for Michigan State, Utah, and Texas. He went undrafted this year and signed with the San Francisco 49ers, but was waived last week. He was first-team All-Pac 12 in 2023 and second-team All-Big 12 in 2024. Special teams has been a longstanding problem for Sean McVay, so maybe Bouwmeester just gives L.A. more options moving forward, and maybe if Evans is dealing with any issues, he gives the team a punter for the rest of the preseason. Ethan Evans needs to get more hang time on his punts. It's been an issue since his rookie season…he gets good distance, but he puts so much pressure on the Rams' coverage unit b/c he out-kicks the coverage unit by 15+ yards. — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) August 15, 2026 If the Rams want, they can keep Bouwmeester on their practice squad after final cuts, without counting against their 16-man limit, until they or another team put him on their 53.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Myth busting narratives surrounding Ty Simpson’s NFL debut
summary: It’s true that Los Angeles Rams rookie quarterback aced his first NFL game. The first round pick led LA to a victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday. Simpson was accurate on over 90% of his throws. He demonstrated a level of mobility that is foreign to recent Rams quarterbacks. Simpson’s arm strength was […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams in action during the preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s true that Los Angeles Rams rookie quarterback aced his first NFL game. The first round pick led LA to a victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday . Simpson was accurate on over 90% of his throws . He demonstrated a level of mobility that is foreign to recent Rams quarterbacks. Simpson’s arm strength was a visible notch above Stetson Bennett’s , the other quarterback battling for the backup role behind Matthew Stafford. 120 seconds of Ty Simpson slicing thru the defense 21/25, 190 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs thoughts? pic.twitter.com/Aj7B2M1hs3 — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) August 15, 2026 Was the Rams’ offense with Simpson at the helm world beating? Far from it. Simpson was surrounded by players on the fringes of LA’s roster . It’s a fair critique to say the offense felt overly conservative and dink and dunk. Simpson grew more comfortable and aggressive as Saturday’s game drew on, and we can still discern some important and encouraging metrics from his performance. Let’s bust a few myths from Simpson’s first game: Myth #1: Simpson was captain checkdown Verdict: Somewhat true Simpson’s average depth of target (ADOT) came to 5.3 yards on 25 passes. That is overly conservative by NFL standards. Still, it’s significantly higher Bennett’s metric from the same game (although he was in for only two drives) of 3.2 yards. There is some important context that is needed in order to paint the full picture. We’ll get there. One data point that I’ll go ahead and provide: Simpson did make two throws behind the line of scrimmage that could be skewing the average on a small sample size. One play was targeted seven yards deep into the backfield. Myth #2: Simpson was overly reliant on play action Verdict: False Eight of Simpson’s 25 dropbacks (32%) featured play action. Most of these came early in his appearance and it seemed to be a well-intentioned plan to help the rookie settle in. Simpson had an ADOT of 6.6 yards on play action throws with an adjusted completion rate of 87.5%. Many of these plays were rollouts, which are simplifications to reduce his reads to half the field. The crutch was removed later in the game and the Rams leaned into more traditional drop back passing. Simpson looked comfortable and hung in the pocket to push the ball down the field. So while the Rams used play action early and often as a tool to help the rookie find a rhythm, it wasn’t a crutch or the only reason why Simpson was successful. Myth busted. Ty Simpson zips it to Brennan Presley for a 23-yard pick up. LARvsKC on @NFLnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NomnCI9rqT — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 Myth #3: Simpson didn’t have a single deep throw Verdict: True It’s true that Simpson did not attempt a throw longer than 20 yards down the field. However, he did complete all six of his attempts within the range of 10-19 yards. These plays went for 108 yards total and Simpson earned an “elite” PFF grade of 92.1. His average depth of target on these six throws was 14.7 yards and all were converted for first downs. Would it be comforting to see Simpson throw and complete deep passes this preseason? Absolutely. But we know the intermediate range is an important area in Sean McVay’s offense, and Simpson performed his best in this area. It’s good enough for now. We can check the other box later. Myth #4: Simpson didn’t use the middle of the field Verdict: False Nine of Simpson’s 25 passes (36%) were targeted towards the center of the field. He completed eight for 78 yards with two touchdowns. Included in this bucket, of course, is the screen pass score to running back Dean Connors. This may be an oversimplification, but if there are three areas you can target—left, right, and center—then you’d expect a 33% equal distribution to these areas. 36% is in the ballpark. Myth busted. Ty zips one to CJ! 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/H9uY1ITr2I — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 15, 2026 Myth #5: Simpson’s play wasn’t sustainable Verdict: False Critics will point to the Rams’ heavy usage of play action and designed rollouts and say that the gameplan was tailored for the first-round pick to look successful. That was mostly true early, although Simpson did buck the trend later into the game. If looking to measure and project sustainable quarterback play, the most reliable measure we have is the Pro Football Focus (PFF) passing grade when kept clean. Play under pressure can be volatile and vary year to year. The true test of quarterbacks comes when everything around them goes right. And Simpson played his best football when kept clean. He earned a PFF passing grade of 80.8 and completed 20/22 passes (90.9%) for 185 yards, two scores, and a passer rating of 132.0. His ADOT was 5.4 yards and near his mark for the overall game. There were no big-time throws nor turnover-worthy plays. That clears the bar. Simpson had a history of often generating big-time throws at Alabama. We haven’t seen that production so far in the NFL. That is the next thing we need to see from him—throwing receivers open in the deep area of the field. There are only reasons to be encouraged about Ty Simpson’s first game in the NFL. Are there still some lingering questions that will hopefully get answered over the next two preseason games? Absolutely. But his first effort checked many of the boxes that you want to see from a rookie first-round pick. Growth is not linear. Progress was evident. Whether it will continue remains to be seen.
author: JB Scott

title: C.J. Daniels is no Puka Nacua
summary: Two of the biggest winners in the L.A. Rams preseason opener on Saturday were receivers who didn’t even suit up, which includes Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington, because on Sean McVay’s team it’s not how you play in the preseason but how often you don’t play that really matters. And whereas Brennan Presley and Xavier […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 15: Los Angeles Rams running back Dean Connors (33) and Los Angeles Rams wide receiver CJ Daniels (6) celebrate after a touchdown during the second half against the Kansas City Chiefs on August 15th at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Two of the biggest winners in the L.A. Rams preseason opener on Saturday were receivers who didn’t even suit up, which includes Konata Mumpfield and Jordan Whittington, because on Sean McVay’s team it’s not how you play in the preseason but how often you don’t play that really matters. And whereas Brennan Presley and Xavier Smith were praised as standouts for the Rams among those who suited up against the Chiefs, sixth-round rookie C.J. Daniels was more of “just a guy” in his preseason debut. Since L.A. made one of the best day three picks in NFL Draft history in 2023, it’s become common for fans to compare Rams rookie receivers to Puka Nacua. It happened to Whittington in 2024, Mumpfield in 2025, and Daniels in 2026. None of them are likely to come anywhere near Nacua’s already-historic career as a fifth-round pick, but at least Whittington and Mumpfield have earned enough of McVay’s respect to have graduated out of preseason action. Meanwhile, their gain means that Daniels is up against an even bigger wall to make McVay’s 53-man roster. After catching just two-of-five targets for 18 yards in the first preseason game, Daniels has work ahead of him to climb up the depth chart before final cuts. Some notables who won’t dress for the Rams today: Ronnie Rivers, Konata Mumpfield & Jordan Whittington, Josiah Stewart, Tyler Davis, and Josh Wallace. We’ll talk about their roles and those who have a chance to claim spots on a very tough roster to make right now on… pic.twitter.com/cd9lhqDjUq — J.B. Long (@JB_Long) August 15, 2026 Puka Nacua’s rookie offseason There was nothing unusual about Nacua’s offseason in 2023, the months after he was drafted. Not really. There was hype that Nacua may be a diamond in the rough, but that’s typical. Fans, media, they do that with dozens, or even hundreds of rookies every year. It doesn’t matter that much. When it really started to matter was after Nacua’s preseason debut. It was August 12, 2023, and Nacua caught three passes for 32 yards with a touchdown against the L.A. Chargers . Fittingly, Nacua was also catching passes from Stetson Bennett, as Daniels did for a short time on Saturday. The touchdown isn’t what matters though. Not really. It’s what happened afterwards: McVay didn’t let Puka Nacua dress for the rest of the preseason. He had earned his stripes. McVay showed fans through actions, not words, that Nacua would be L.A.‘s WR2 when Cooper Kupp was healthy, and WR1 when he wasn’t. That’s what you call a real diamond in the rough , not just offseason hype. In Nacua’s NFL debut, he was targeted 15 times. The receivers compared to Nacua in the years since? They’re lucky to be targeted more than 15 times in an entire season. And Daniels, unfortunately for him, is now firmly situated behind the two receivers who got into McVay’s system earlier than him and have been graduated from preseason reps. Konata Mumpfield rising In L.A.’s first depth chart of the month, Whittington and Mumpfield were on the second-string depth chart behind Nacua and Davante Adams . This was reaffirmed by McVay’s decision to not let either of them suit up on Saturday. The top-4 wide receivers on the depth chart is undeniable: Puka Nacua Davante Adams Konata Mumpfield Jordan Whittington Mumpfield and Whittington could be interchangeable, but they are definitely in the 3-4 slots. But Mumpfield also got an endorsement from Adams in the offseason , something the veteran receiver has rarely done for young receivers. He doesn’t really like praising players and giving them a big ego, but Adams has been a little more public than usual about his admiration for Mumpfield. There’s also the chance that because Whittington has had more time to prove himself, but didn’t really get better in 2025, that Mumpfield has the higher ceiling and more room to grow. Whittington had 18 catches for 171 yards in 2025, whereas Mumpfield had 10 catches for 92 yards. Both not good numbers, especially in terms of yards per catch. Xavier Smith was better than both of them combined. Players like Daniels and Pressley certainly do not have to climb over Terrell Owens and Jerry Rice to get the WR3 spot. That’s not in dispute: This doesn’t mean that Whittington and Mumpfield are better than Daniels. It doesn’t mean that Daniels couldn’t move up the depth chart by the end of the year, if not sooner. We’re talking about a role that will continue to be up for grabs—partially because it’s also just not that important. Don’t forget 12 and 13 Personnel Other Rams who didn’t play on Saturday include Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson, Terrance Ferguson, and Davis Allen. Max Klare got his fair share of playing time. With Nacua and Adams playing the vast majority of snaps in 12 personnel (1 RB, 2 TE, 2 WR), there won’t be much time for Whittington, Mumpfield, or Daniels, while they’re healthy. But it also means that the WR5 or WR6 essentially needs to be a special teamer . And a good one. The Rams will probably play Ferguson a lot more snaps than they play WR3, and especially WR4 (who will barely play), meaning that Daniels has yet another obstacle to clear before he’s ever seen on the field. It certainly isn’t going to happen as fast as it did for Nacua, and frankly in this league, the last thing coaches are known for…is patience. Daniels could be WR7 right now We’ve established that Nacua and Adams are 1 and 2, and we should by now all agree that Whittington and Mumpfield are moving up to 3 and 4, leaving a battle for WR5-6-7. We also know that it’s unlikely a WR7 makes the roster. Daniels caught two passes, and his three incomplete targets can’t all be blamed on him. Here, he makes a fine contested catch in the middle of the field for his best play of the day: As the game progressed, you really saw Ty Simpson start to get comfortable. With be interested if Rams let him off the reigns a little bit next week. Tight coverage on CJ Daniels and Simpson throws an accurate ball. pic.twitter.com/ZPOUISGzac — Blaine Grisak 💭 (@BGMediaOnSI) August 16, 2026 That’s all well and good. But in this league, you make your own luck. Coaches don’t have sympathy for “well it’s not my fault” excuses. Everything is your fault. That’s called accountability. Get open more often. Demand attention. If you’re undeniable, you can’t be denied. Pressley had a better game as a receiver. Xavier Smith had a better game as a receiver. Klare had a better game as a receiver. These are not opinions. These are facts. What could be an opinion is that C.J. Daniels blocked his ass off and is trying to earn a spot by being a good player when he’s not being targeted: CJ Daniels only had 2 catches today, but what stood out to me was the blocking. He was in the shit, putting hands on people, I was impressed with him today and I understand why the Rams drafted him. — hyperNight (@hyprnight) August 16, 2026 That will certainly put y0u in McVay’s good graces too. Although, it won’t matter if Whittington and Mumpfield are also good blockers. Then what’s separating you from them in a positive way? More cost-controlled years on your contract, maybe. Daniels said all the right things after the game, calling the preseason an “opportunity for young guys” and practice squad guys to show what they can do. He had a few chances to do that and he did almost all that was asked of him, for which he deserves accolades and attention and more chances in the future. A solid first outing for the rookies in the @RamsNFL preseason opener against the Chiefs. After the game, our @DarrenMHaynes caught up with wide receiver CJ Daniels about the opportunity to show what they're capable of…
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Upon further review: Brennan Presley’s big day
summary: Brennan Presley had one of the most productive games of any player in the Los Angeles Rams’ 20-12 preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs Saturday. In what will be an uphill climb to make the roster, it was a strong first step for the former Oklahoma State Cowboy. As a speedy but especially small […]
full_text: Brennan Presley had one of the most productive games of any player in the Los Angeles Rams’ 20-12 preseason win over the Kansas City Chiefs Saturday . In what will be an uphill climb to make the roster, it was a strong first step for the former Oklahoma State Cowboy. As a speedy but especially small wide receiver (standing just 5-foot-8, 174 pounds), Presley is going to get pigeonholed as a straight-line, gadget player, whether that’s fair or unfair. If he’s going to climb the depth chart and sneak onto the 53-man roster, he’ll need to both show a multidimensional skill set on offense and make a positive impact on special teams. Presley did a great job showing off both of those things against the Chiefs. First, the offensive production. Stats aren’t especially useful during preseason action, as the great Daniel Jeremiah explained this weekend . Still, when you see a player like Presley post a game-high four receptions for 58 yards, it’s at least worth taking note of. That’s especially true in his case because he showed he can win in multiple ways. First, a gimme in space allowing him to use that plus speed. While the Rams have a multitude of things they need to see out of both Stetson Bennett and Ty Simpson this preseason, getting both of them easy completions and explosives is important too. This was a great call from offensive coordinator Nathan Scheelhaase, who took over play-calling responsibilities for this game. The run action took the defense to the right while Presley, aligned wing right, scraped across to the left. This would have been a chunk gain regardless, but Presley’s speed allowed him to fly past defensive back Chris Rowland-Wallace and inside the red zone. This is the kind of play Presley should dominate with, given his athletic profile. That, in turn, is why the following play is so vital. Matthew Stafford is not afraid to throw over the middle. He will push the ball with deep in-breakers all day. The Rams, generally speaking, want to push the ball. The fact that Presley is able to get open on a deep in and make an athletic play to snatch the ball and regain his footing is encouraging. We don’t have the benefit of all-22 view as of press time, but the end result for Presley is a positive. He was a practice squad piece last season and only made an appearance in one actual game, but this is one of college football’s all-time leading receivers . He’s capable of producing, but after playing exactly zero offensive snaps in 2025 and averaging under 10 yards per reception during his last two seasons in Stillwater, he needs to keep proving he’s a real receiver and not just a gadget player. As mentioned above, special teams will also be crucial for Presley if he wants to make this team out of camp. Anyone who can do anything positive on special teams is a boon for the Rams, and he had a couple nice kick returns of Saturday. L.A.’s beleaguered special teams finished 28 th in the NFL in total EPA last season. The only teams who finished worse were the Falcons, Raiders, Cardinals and Saints. None of those teams were close to good last season, and the Rams have to be better in the third phase this year. A low-cost return man who shows here that he can both make tacklers miss and get to the edge thanks to his speed is an intriguing option at the absolute bare minimum. This isn’t intended to make Presley out to be a roster lock. There are a limited number of spots for receivers on this roster, and there’s an abundance of competition for the final spot in that room. Still, if we’re going to treat the preseason as a chance for fringe players to make their case for a full-time roster spot, this was as good of a first impression as he could have made this summer.
author: Brendan Dzwierzynski

title: Good, Bad and Ugly: Ty Simpson, defense showed out in KC
summary: The Los Angeles Rams came away victorious in their preseason opener with a 20-12 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday. LA put together a strong showing in Kansas City, as Ty Simpson and the defense showed out this weekend. Here is the good, the bad and the ugly from the Rams’ preseason matchup […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Ty Simpson #15 of the Los Angeles Rams hands the football to x27 during the first quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams came away victorious in their preseason opener with a 20-12 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday. LA put together a strong showing in Kansas City, as Ty Simpson and the defense showed out this weekend. Here is the good, the bad and the ugly from the Rams’ preseason matchup against the Chiefs. The Good Ty Simpson shut up critics … for a week Thank goodness Simpson had a great game, or social media would’ve been insufferable postgame. Social media’s already that way, but I digress. In the first couple weeks of preseason, many high-profile rookie quarterbacks have stood out and posted quality, efficient outings, effectively putting pressure on Simpson’s debut. Instead, Simpson might’ve had the best rookie QB showing so far in preseason. #Rams QB Ty Simpson looked real smooth in his preseason debut — 21 of 25 for 190 yards and 2 TDs pic.twitter.com/dq5H8qE3FZ — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 16, 2026 The Rams’ coaching staff and fanbase could not have asked for a better performance from the first-year signal caller. While most of Simpson’s work came against third- and fourth-stringers, it really didn’t seem to matter. He put together an efficient performance and looked quite poised in the process. Again, you truly couldn’t have asked for a better debut. Now, there’s going to be a lot of ridiculous comparisons for the next week over who’s better between Simpson and top overall pick Fernando Mendoza. We all knew this would happen too, as for whatever reason, people put far too much stock in preseason games. Praise the football gods the Rams were on the right side of it this time. For at least a week, Simpson shut up critics of him and LA for making the pick. Defense played lights out It cannot be overstated enough that Saturday’s game against the Chiefs was only preseason, and backups primarily played. That shouldn’t take away from how good the defense played. If Simpson was the hero of the game, the unit was a worthy sidekick. While Kansas City converted nearly half of their third down opportunities, they were held to just 314 yards and 0-for-3 on red zone opportunities. Holding the Chiefs to only four field goals is a sign that the Rams have some quality depth, which will be much-needed if this year goes as long as they hope. Additionally, KC’s three quarterbacks: Justin Fields, rookie Garrett Nussmeier and fifth-year signal caller Chris Oladokun were held to 189 yards passing and 5.9 yards per attempt. Not a bad day at the offense for Chris Shula’s unit. Young playmakers stood out What a game for the young playmakers in this one, and I’m not just talking about Simpson! Undrafted running back Dean Connors is making a name for himself after catching both of Simpson’s touchdown passes. Connors added 22 rushing yards, proving that he can be a valuable all-around depth piece at the position. He’ll be a hard one to keep off the 53-man roster, that’s for sure. Dean Connors gets the first touchdown of the game 💪 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYp8K pic.twitter.com/JMKl83IZfn — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 15, 2026 Fellow undrafted wide receiver — from the 2025 class — Brennan Presley led the team with 58 yards on four receptions, including a 23-yard dart early in the game. The Rams have a clear hole at the WR3 position behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, so if he continues showing out, he can easily step into that role during the season. Presley led the team in receiving yards, while rookie tight end Max Klare led LA with seven receptions. The Ohio State product was a key target for Simpson, who went to him often. That will be a tandem to watch, not only this preseason, but in the post-Matthew Stafford era. It was a blast watching those youngsters stand out and earn so much playing time. Les Snead sure knows how to pick them, doesn’t he? The Bad Stetson Bennett’s future NFL chances While all eyes were on Simpson’s debut, Stetson Bennett did nothing to stand out. Isn’t that the perfect way to describe his NFL career? He didn’t have a terrible showing, as he competed four of his six pass attempts for 38 yards. Bennett led a field goal drive following a punt on the game’s opening possession, but that was it before Simpson took over for the remainder of the game. The punt came after he threw behind CJ Daniels on a third down slant. There was nothing special about his outing whatsoever, and that’s not a great thing. It’s fair to say that Bennett is playing for far more than being Stafford’s backup. He’s playing for his NFL future , and should he lose out to Simpson despite his years in the offense, it’s doubtful that many teams will request his services, even if they’re desperate. Backup or not, Bennett should look much better than he has this many years into his NFL career. His best football days were likely in college. The Ugly Rams lose backup option to injury early Rams offensive tackle Keagen Trost was lost to injury early in the game, and that’s not great for the team’s depth. Trost, the rookie out of Missouri, was ruled out with a hamstring injury early after leaving the game in the first quarter. He is currently projected as the backup to Warren McClendon Jr. ahead of the season, so leaving him is a big deal. The severity of the injury is unknown. Anyone who’s ever watched the NFL before, or has experienced it themselves, understands how nagging a hamstring injury can be. Hopefully, Trost can return reasonably soon, as he’s likely set to be a key piece of the Rams’ offensive depth in 2026. Aaron Donald rumors This isn’t exactly connected to the preseason opener, yet it’s taking away the glow from an otherwise promising Rams showing. Simply put, the constant Aaron Donald rumors are distracting and must end. Sean McVay isn’t putting a deadline on Donald’s potential return, but maybe he should. Rams HC Sean McVay says he won’t put an “invisible deadline” on Aaron Donald to come out of retirement but added that he hopes the former star defensive tackle makes a decision “sooner than later.” https://t.co/jD4uj4i9bR — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 16, 2026 Deciding whether to return to the NFL after years away is a big decision. It’s understandable why it’s taken so long. However, when will it end? These rumors are driving me crazy! AD, love you buddy, but make a decision already or stay the hell home. The Rams have a season to prep for and cannot afford any distractions ahead of another potential championship run.
author: Evan Craig

title: Rams PFF Grades: Stetson Bennett finished last on offense
summary: Pro Football Focus (PFF) published the Los Angeles Rams’ first grades of the 2026 season. LA earned an exhibition victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday. The highlight, of course, was first-round quarterback Ty Simpson’s debut. PFF was kind to him in their grading, and there is more to come on that. After each […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams throws a first quarter pass during the NFL preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pro Football Focus (PFF) published the Los Angeles Rams’ first grades of the 2026 season. LA earned an exhibition victory over the Kansas City Chiefs on Saturday. The highlight, of course, was first-round quarterback Ty Simpson’s debut. PFF was kind to him in their grading, and there is more to come on that. After each game at Turf Show Times we post an immediate reaction to who performed well and who didn’t. We call it “winners & losers” . Within the next 24 hours we post the PFF grades, of which serves as an objective form of the same topic. Who earned top marks on Saturday? Let’s dive in. Top five grades on offense: 1 – Austin Blaske, LG: 80.9 Blaske earned his best grade in run blocking at 80.3. He also fared well in pass protection with a mark of 76.9. Blaske played all 54 offensive snaps at left guard. Not a bad day at the office for the rookie UDFA out of North Carolina. He’s someone to keep on eye on over the remaining two games. 2 – Brennan Presley, WR: 79.6 Last season’s preseason star, Brennan Presley, is doing it again. He led LA in receiving yards with 58 on four receptions. 39 of his yards came after the catch point, and he averaged 9.8 yards after the catch. Presley is a small receiver and does not really fit into the Rams’ prototype. One sign of this was his poor run blocking grade of 58.8. He’s someone that needs a look at punt returner, and someone receiver-needy teams should keep an eye on. Ty Simpson zips it to Brennan Presley for a 23-yard pick up. LARvsKC on @NFLnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/NomnCI9rqT — NFL (@NFL) August 15, 2026 3 – Ty Simpson, QB: 78.1 Simpson took 25 of LA’s 31 total dropbacks. He played an immaculately clean game with an adjusted completion rate of 91.3%. There were a lot of short throws; however, Simpson got better as the game went on and the aggression and true drop backs (no play action) grew more frequent late. Simpson finished with 21 completions on 25 passes (84.0%) for 190 yards and two touchdowns. Of all the 2026 rookie quarterbacks, Simpson currently ranks third in PFF grading behind Carson Beck (Cardinals) and Drew Allar (Steelers). He’s second behind Joe Fagnano (Ravens) in yards and tied for the lead in touchdowns. Ty zips one to CJ! 📺 @CBSLosAngeles | 📲 https://t.co/R5m5kJYWYi pic.twitter.com/H9uY1ITr2I — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 15, 2026 4 – Beaux Limmer, RG: 74.4 It’s not surprising to see Limmer crack the top five. He played 34 snaps at right guard and performed very well in pass blocking with a mark of 84.4. His run grade was weaker at 68.7. 5 – Mark Redman, TE: 73.9 Redman played 19 snaps. Five came in the run game and he earned a blocking grade of 58.7. Not great. His best production came as a receiver where he caught all three of his targets for 47 yards. Redman earned 13 yards after the catch point and was one of the more vertical targets on the day with an ADOT of 11.3 yards. Ty Simpson boot to Mark Redman!!! pic.twitter.com/9EDmEjQdxo — Allen Sales (@AllenSales) August 15, 2026 Other notes on offense Of the 22 players to make an appearance on offense, Stetson Bennett finished in last place in the PFF grading. Bennett had an anemic average depth of target (ADOT) of 3.2 yards versus Simpson at 5.3. The veteran was credited with two missed throws on six attempts. He was only pressured once. Is the preseason quarterback battle already over after a single game? Top five grades on defense: 1 – Zech McPhearson, CB: 80.7 The Rams recently signed McPhearson, who spent the last few years with the Eagles. He almost earned a pick that was later ruled incomplete. Most of his snaps came later in the game in relief of Al’zillion Hamilton. McPhearson did not allow a single completion and recorded a pass breakup. It may not have counted but huge play from #Rams CB Zech McPhearson. He barely joined the roster and made some noise already. — James Brizuela (@james_brizuela) August 15, 2026 2 – Cam Lampkin, CB: 68.2 The overall grading was not great on defense. 68.2 would not usually crack the top five during the regular season. Lampkin did not have a good game. He allowed catches on all three of his targets for 30 yards and a passer rating of 108.3. 3 – Alex Cook, FS: 64.5 Cook made four tackles and was sure-handed. He did not miss an attempt and earned a tackling grade of 78.2. 4 – Ty Hamilton, DT: 64.4 Ty Hamilton played just 19 snaps. He came on late last season and played important snaps during the playoffs. He continues to struggle as a run defender (57.3) but can contribute as a pass rusher. He recorded one pressure. 5 – Al’zillion Hamilton, CB: 63.9 Hamilton missed a tackle on four attempts. His best contributions came in coverage where he allowed three receptions on five targets for 27 yards (16 after the catch) and a long of 17. He recorded a pass breakup and allowed a passer rating of 74.6. Hamilton came off the field with roughly 20 defensive snaps to go, so we could assume he’s ahead of McPhearson and Lampkin on the depth chart. Other notes on defense While rookie Tim Keenan finished with five tackles and a sack, he finished towards the back of the pack on defense and ranked 19th of the 22 players. He earned a run defense mark of 39.3 and a tackling grade of 28.8. He missed a tackle on six opportunities.
author: JB Scott

title: Rams preseason snap counts: What we learned for 53-man roster
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have been consistent in their approach to the preseason in the past decade under Sean McVay. We know this will be a very competitive roster to make. There may only be a few spots up for grabs on the margins. Sometimes McVay’s most telling move is who sits out. There were […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Running back Jarquez Hunter #27 of the Los Angeles Rams carries the ball during the 1st quarter of the preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Jamie Squire/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have been consistent in their approach to the preseason in the past decade under Sean McVay. We know this will be a very competitive roster to make. There may only be a few spots up for grabs on the margins. Sometimes McVay’s most telling move is who sits out. There were a couple of interesting inactives on Saturday against the Kansas City Chiefs that should inform 53-man roster projections. Let’s summarize everything we learned from the preseason opener in Kansas City. An injury to keep an eye on Keagen Trost, RT Trost started at right tackle before leaving in the first quarter with a hamstring injury . It seems the Rams are preparing Trost to backup Warren McClendon, which means veteran David Quessenberry is likely the backup to Alaric Jackson amid the starter’s potential suspension. Should Trost miss extended time, he is a candidate to start the regular season on injured reserve. This would open up an opportunity for players like AJ Arcuri to stick with the team. Did not play – probably safe Shaun Dolac, MLB No surprises here. Dolac was playing more on defense towards the end of last season before suffering an injury and missing the playoffs. He’s also one of LA’s more important special teams contributors. It’s noteworthy that Dolac has gone from one of the highest volume participants of the preseason a year ago to safe in 2026. Grant Stuard, MLB It didn’t really make sense that LA would cut their free agent investment in special teams. Stuard did not play Saturday and that confirms he’s safe. Josh Wallace, CB It will be interesting to see how often the Rams deploy Trent McDuffie in the slot. Consequently, how different will Quentin Lake’s role be in 2026? LA is set at the first two slot corner spots. Wallace is third on the depth chart but seems safe to make the team. Tyler Davis, DT Davis continues to be one of the most underrated names on the Rams’ roster. He was on the sidelines dressed in street clothes along with Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske. There will not be a surprise cut of Davis this year. Did not play – interesting data point All three of these players sat out in Kansas City; however, this isn’t a clear sign that they are locks to make the roster. All have years of preseason experience with the Rams. What else is there to learn from additional time on the field? The Rams know who these players are at this point. Ronnie Rivers, RB Probably ahead of Jarquez Hunter on the depth chart. Rivers also contributes on special teams with higher frequency than Hunter, although that mix could change this season potentially. Davis Allen, TE Listed as a co-starter on the team’s unofficial depth chart. Max Klare isn’t getting cut as a second-round pick. Can the Rams really keep five tight ends? If they do, it truly signals that LA will again be deploying heavier personnel and fewer receivers may stick on the 53-man roster as a result. AJ Arcuri, OT The Rams should not have much confidence in Quessenberry if he must step in because of a Jackson suspension. It would be wise to keep as many options available as possible. Trost starting at right tackle could signal that the team is not overly concerned about Jackson getting suspended, and generally front offices have an understanding of expectations that is not publicly available. Do the Rams feel they have nothing new to learn about Arcuri or is he too important to subject to injury risk? Played surprisingly late into the game Desjuan Johnson, EDGE Johnson is currently LA’s fourth EDGE. It’s a position where numbers are needed because they are often rotated. I’d lean towards Johnson being safe, although it was surprising to see him play almost the entire game Saturday. Cam Lampkin, CB With Wallace sitting out the contest, Lampkin is probably unlikely to make this team. We saw Lampkin play in the slot and last preseason he mainly aligned outside. Considering the positive training camp reports that Lampkin was causing turnovers left and right, he did not perform up to that standard versus the Chiefs. Max Klare, TE There are two ways to read Klare participating the entire game. He is either on the same developmental plan as Ty Simpson and the Rams don’t expect him to contribute much in 2026, barring injury. Or the team knows they need as many tight ends as possible and felt a high volume of both snaps and targets could accelerate his growth trajectory. I lean more towards the first idea at this point.
author: JB Scott

title: Ty Simpson compared to Baker Mayfield after 1 preseason game
summary: People have ways of hedging their bets when it comes to highly-touted quarterbacks in the preseason, and Ty Simpson’s successful debut for the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday was prime real estate for hedging. You see, if Simpson played poorly, then believers would say “It’s only the preseason, who cares?” and skeptics would say, “I […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - AUGUST 15: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Ty Simpson (15) behind the line during the second half against the Kansas City Chiefs on August 15th at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by William Purnell/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images People have ways of hedging their bets when it comes to highly-touted quarterbacks in the preseason, and Ty Simpson’s successful debut for the Los Angeles Rams on Saturday was prime real estate for hedging. You see, if Simpson played poorly, then believers would say “It’s only the preseason, who cares?” and skeptics would say, “I told you so.” After Simpson played well enough to earn almost-universal praise, then skeptics say “It’s only the preseason, who cares?” and believers say, “I told you so.” That’s just how it works. It’s how it’s always worked. And nobody’s wrong. And nobody’s right. 120 seconds of Ty Simpson slicing thru the defense 21/25, 190 yards, 2 TDs, 0 INTs thoughts? pic.twitter.com/Aj7B2M1hs3 — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) August 15, 2026 Football fans have always felt like they have a personal relationship with quarterbacks and the emotions cause logic to be discarded as a distraction when it fails to support their priors. I call it the “Varsity Blues syndrome”. Everybody knows Varsity Blues. When Paul Walker’s character is healthy, James Van Der Beek’s character is worthless. Even his own father despises him. When Walker breaks his leg, their worlds are completely reversed. It’s not logical. It’s football. Well, I have no dog in the fight. I have always watched football objectively, or at least, that’s the goal. I’m not void of emotions, but I think desire gets in the way of objective reality and I really hate that. So you can believe me or not, but this is what I think of Simpson’s first game with the Rams: It was totally fine. It’s the type of preseason game that could be had by a quarterback who becomes a Pro Bowl star. And it’s the type of preseason game that could be had by an athletically-gifted career backup. In terms of predicting the future off of Simpson’s one preseason game… you can’t. I know many onlookers have already done that, and many more will try, but it’s all just words right now. It’s all fantasy. It’s the script for a movie. Maybe that movie is Varsity Blues. And maybe you’re the star, and maybe you’re not, but it can all change on a single play. However, I still wouldn’t hedge my bets on a preseason game. I told you so. Rams’ top pick Simpson shines in 2-TD preseason debut vs. Chiefs ( ESPN ) “I thought he took what the defense gave him,” McVay said. “I thought he read the plays out, read with his feet. I thought he did a really good job overall. … I thought he kept the ball in play. That’s the biggest thing, is keeping the ball in play.” Though he didn’t know what to expect going into his first NFL game, Simpson said that after the first drive that it felt “just like playing in the backyard.” Simpson is the first player with 190 passing yards and two touchdown passes in his preseason debut since Baker Mayfield did it with the Cleveland Browns in 2018, according to ESPN Research. Simpson completed passes to seven players, and both of his touchdown passes went to running back Dean Connors . Ty Simpson dazzles in his Rams debut ( PFT ) McVay may be smiling, too, if he thinks the rookie can be trusted to serve as the understudy to reigning MVP Matthew Stafford. The only other option is Stetson Bennett, who has no regular-season snaps in three seasons. Ideally, the preseason will be Simpson’s only chance to get live reps. That likely explains the decision to give him three full quarters of playing time. But it’s not just development for a post-Stafford future. They need to have someone ready, in the event Stafford’s back flares up or he has some other injury during the grind of a 17-game season. Rams’ First-Rounder Ty Simpson Delivered An Impressive Preseason Debut vs. Chiefs ( FOX ) Simpson’s first score came from a quick four-play drive, where he found rookie running back Dean Connors for a nine-yard touchdown pass. Shortly after, Simpson led the Rams on an eight-play drive that resulted in a second touchdown throw to Connors, securing the Rams’ win over Kansas City. While the majority of Simpson’s training camp experience was spent playing behind quarterback Stetson Bennett for second-team reps, his preseason entrance allowed him the chance to showcase his skillset. Additionally, Simpson has had the chance to learn from MVP quarterback Matthew Stafford , who’s entering his 17th year in the NFL and his fifth season with the Rams. Sean McVay on Aaron Donald comeback: ‘We’re not at that point quite yet’ ( LA Times ) People are desperate for the Donald story to come to a conclusion, but McVay has no update—and he never really has had one. 5 Takeaways from Rams’ 20-12 preseason Week 1 win over Chiefs ( RAMS ) 4) Klare a reliable target: Targeted a team-high eight times, Klare finished with seven receptions for 37 yards – much of those from Simpson – displaying the skillset that made him look like a great fit alongside the returning personnel at tight end. 4 Winners and 3 Losers From Rams’ Preseason Win Over Chiefs ( SI ) Loser: QB Stetson Bennett On that note, Bennett’s stock definitely took a hit. Bennett didn’t necessarily play poorly, but his first pass landed behind wide receiver CJ Daniels on a short slant. His final pass of the afternoon was almost intercepted as he lofted a pass short in the end zone intended for Max Klare. Bennett was efficient out of play action and on the move, but there was a clear difference in the two quarterbacks. Accuracy and putting the ball in harm’s way have always been issues for Bennett. How a rookie and a punt returner secured the Rams’ win in Arrowhead ( The Sporting Tribune ) The backyard in Martin, Tennessee. Population small; dreams large. His first drive ended in a punt. Three plays. Three-and-out. The second drive was a different song. Simpson completed four consecutive passes for 41 yards, moving the chains with the patience of a man who understands rhythm isn’t given; it is earned. Harrison Mevis, the “Thicker Kicker” who can split the wings off a fly, drilled a 40-yard field goal through the uprights. Comment of the Day: From JB’s Winners and Losers, by delusionalramfanslosteve “Agree on Simpson 100%! It’s just the first step but he showed he belongs. I think Klare will get as many reps as possible, getting him ready to play as soon as possible. I think he and Ferguson will be the receiving TEs and the others will play inline. Conners and Andersen showed some legit stuff as well. I’ll be kind of bummed if Desjuan doesn’t make the team. Dude’s been a good Ram.“ Feed Post: Keagen Trost injured in debut

title: The candidates who’ll lead the Raiders in scoring this season
summary: It was but a mere glimpse, but what an encouraging view of Klint Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders offense in the preseason opener, no? A mix of both efficiency and staples of the Kubiak scheme, the Silver & Black’s head coach and offensive play caller provided a window into what he’s cooking up this season in […]
full_text: Nov 2, 2025; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (2) runs the ball during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It was but a mere glimpse, but what an encouraging view of Klint Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders offense in the preseason opener, no? A mix of both efficiency and staples of the Kubiak scheme, the Silver & Black’s head coach and offensive play caller provided a window into what he’s cooking up this season in Las Vegas’ 27-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals this past Thursday. The opening drive showcases the ever-efficient Kirk Cousins in the driver seat as the veteran quarterback and looking sharp pacing a 10-play, 68-yard touchdown drive. Behind an offensive line that kept him clean and comfortable, Cousins went 5-of-6 for 50 yards with his touchdown pass going to tight end Michael Mayer. It was a script featuring the heavy personnel packages — multiple tight ends — a (gasp!) fullback in Connor Heyward, pre-snap motions, and balanced air and ground attacks. It wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows, of course. And Kubiak — a rookie head coach — admitted as much in the post-game press conference. “I think the thing that stands out to me, analytically or not, is our penalties. We really hurt ourselves,” the Raiders head coach said. “We put ourselves in some negative situations, and that’s not winning football. Offensively, the fact that we didn’t turn the ball over is always good. That’s something that didn’t stand out last night, but offensively, you can’t go into a half a football and not score points. So, we didn’t help the defense there. We weren’t playing team football in that second half.” With the initial preseason tilt in the box and two more left on slate before Week 1 of the regular season, let’s dive into the candidates to lead the Raiders in scoring in 2026. Las Vegas finished dead last in the league in terms of points scored (241 total) and yards gained (4,168 total), so the bar is set quite low for Kubiak. There’s a high likelihood his offense won’t finish 32nd out of the 32 teams, though. So let’s take a look at who led the team in points in 2025 before jumping into this coming season: By The Numbers Raiders 2025 Scoring Leaders No. 1: Daniel Carlson, kicker, 87 points No. 2: Ashton Jeanty, running back, 60 points No. 3: Brock Bowers, tight end, 44 points No. 4: Tre Tucker, wide receiver, 30 points No. 5: Shedrick Jackson, wide receiver, 6 points Rookie Ashton Jeanty. pic.twitter.com/rM3XVsFk3C — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) July 12, 2026 Status Quo Let’s get this out of the way first and foremost: The winner of the Raiders’ kicking competition between grizzled veteran Matt Gay and undrafted free agent Kansei Matsuzawa will lead the Silver & Black in scoring this coming season. With Gay being steady in training camp practices and the Tokyo Toe having issues in both said camp sessions and hitting the upright on his lone field goal attempt in the preseason opener, the veteran has the edge. There’s still plenty of practices and two more exhibition slates before Week 1, however. Come to think of it, I’ll just hedge things here: Whomever is the Raiders’ place kicker come Week 1 will be the scoring leader this coming season. The reason why kickers pace NFL teams in scoring is due to the fac they handle both extra points and field goals giving them the supreme advantage to stockpile points. That sole credit is the key as an extra point counts as one point and field goals count for three points. That high volume is often unmatched by other skill positions. As you can see from the Top 5 above, Carlson paced Las Vegas’ scoring summary. The Fantastic Four With the obvious out of the way, let’s look at the other four that’ll are likely to lead the Raiders in scoring: No. 2: Jeanty No. 3: Bowers No. 4: Michael Mayer, tight end No. 5: Jalen Nailor, wide receiver While Jeanty didn’t eclipse 1,000-yards rushing as a rookie last season, he did find the end zone a total of 10 times — five on the ground and five more through the air. Kubiak spoke about maximizing Jeanty in his offense and if that does ring true, expect the No. 6 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft to be an active ball carrier and pass catcher this coming season. A similar 10-touchdown total or more means eclipsing the 60 total points he put up as a rookie. “Like we talked about earlier, the more that we can do, the better it’s going to be. He goes out there every single day in special teams period and he’s working all the routes and trying to get better,” Raiders running backs coach Omar Young said of Jeanty. “I know he talked about that as being one of his goals in the offseason to go attack that process of being a better route runner.” Raiders linebacker Nakobe Dean on practicing against TE Brock Bowers: “He made us expeditiously better at the University of Georgia. Me, Quay Walker, and Eric Stokes.” 🎥: @MikeDixon_VST #RaiderNation | #Raiders pic.twitter.com/bRoKWI3i46 — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) August 4, 2026 Then there’s Bowers who is having a terrific training camp and is at a clean bill of health heading into Year 3 at just 23 years old (the tight end turns 24 on December 13). Hauling in seven touchdowns in 2025 as the de facto WR1 for Las Vegas, the expectation is Bowers will once again be the top option in Kubiak’s aerial attack this coming season. Able to line up as a traditional in-line tight end, in the slot, or even on the perimeter as a boundary receiver, the Georgia product has the size, route running, and speed to be a complete nightmare for opposing defenses. That all said, I wouldn’t be surprised if Bowers tops Jeanty in terms of points scored in 2026. Bowers’ seven touchdowns and a two-point conversion gave him 44 last year and having more in Kubiak’s offense is highly plausible. “Brock is highly, highly intelligent football player. He’s such a natural player and a sneaky player. Some people were born to play football, and I think he was one of them,” Raiders tight end coach Luke Steckel said of his unicorn tight end. “I think you could put a blindfold on him, and he’d find a way to get open. He just has such a great feel for space out there versus zone coverage. He’s got great release plans versus man-to-man when they want to come down and press him. But it all starts with the mental aspect, like you’re alluding to. He’s an extremely smart player, but he also puts in the work. He studies all night, all morning.” Fellow tight end Mayer is a sneaky player himself as he has size to be a blocker but surprising speed and soft hands to be a trusted target in the red zone. While he’s only hauled in three touchdowns in his first three years in the league, Mayer heads into the final leg of his rookie contract and has all the skills that Kubiak seeks in his tight ends. And with the coach loving multiple tight end sets, the 25-year-old Notre Dame product has a chance to have his most productive season since being taken in the second round (35th overall) of the 2023 draft. Lastly, Nailor. While a plenty of projections have Tucker finishing in the Top 5 of points scored for the Raiders in 2026 — he did have five touchdowns last season — Nailor, a free agent-addition from the Minnesota Vikings has an opportunity to become a trusted target in Las Vegas. The 5-foot-11 and 199-pound Nevada native offers speed from both the slot and outside and hauled in four touchdowns in 2025 and, before that, six in 2024. A heady route runner that can create separation quickly, the 27-year-old can excel as both a deep threat and red zone nuisance.

full_text: LONDON, ENGLAND - OCTOBER 8: Foley Fatukasi of Jacksonville Jaguars looks on during the NFL match between Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on October 8, 2023 in London, England. (Photo by Vincent Mignott/DeFodi Images via Getty Images) | DeFodi Images via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders lost their first preseason game of the season on Thursday Night. One of the reasons for the loss was the struggles to stop the run. In a move to add depth to the defensive tackle position, the Raiders looked to the free-agent market for help. They signed former Houston Texan Folorunso Fatukasi to join the Silver and Black on Saturday. Fatukasi is a big run defender with 124 career run stops, according to PFF. He has started to fall off in play over the last couple of seasons, now that he’s 30. However, he will add beef inside to help stop the run, which is detrimental as the game slowly moves back to a run-first league. In a corresponding move, the Raiders put Brennen Jackson on injury reserve. He was earning reps with the ones in training camp and was a big blow to roster depth. title: Quinn Ewers suffers groin injury in Dolphins loss to Commanders
summary: Miami Dolphins quarterback Quinn Ewers sustained a groin injury in the team’s preseason loss to the Washington Commanders on Friday. The injury reportedly occurred early in the game, but Ewers, the team’s second-string quarterback, played through it until he was rotated out of the game for third-string passer Cam Miller. The Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson […]
full_text: Aug 14, 2026; Landover, Maryland, USA; Miami Dolphins quarterback Quinn Ewers (14) passes the ball as Washington Commanders linebacker Joshua Josephs (48) rushes during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins quarterback Quinn Ewers sustained a groin injury in the team’s preseason loss to the Washington Commanders on Friday. The injury reportedly occurred early in the game, but Ewers, the team’s second-string quarterback, played through it until he was rotated out of the game for third-string passer Cam Miller. The Miami Herald’s Barry Jackson was the first to report the injury on Sunday. The Dolphins re-signed quarterback Mark Gronowski on Sunday, likely to give Ewers time to recover while adding another passer for training camp practices this week. According to Jackson, Ewers could “miss a few days or a week” due to the injury. Miami is scheduled to host the New York Giants in a joint practice and their second preseason game this week. Ewers had a rough day against the Commanders on Sunday, coming into the game on the Dolphins’ second offensive series after starter Malik Willis led the offense to an opening drive touchdown. Ewers finished with one completion on eight attempts, gaining 27 yards. He threw one interception and finished the game with a 1.6 passer rating. The injury could have played a factor in the struggles and could explain why the 2025 seventh-round pick never appeared comfortable on Friday. Miami will move forward with Willis at the top of the depth chart, with Miller likely taking the second-team reps until Ewers is fully recovered. Gronowski, who started training camp with the Dolphins before being waived last week, will provide depth as the third option.

title: Dolphins bring back QB Mark Gronowski in Sunday roster moves
summary: The Miami Dolphins announced the re-signing of quarterback Mark Gronowski on Sunday, nine days after he had been waived by the team. The return comes a couple of days after Miami’s opening preseason game of the year, a 20-7 loss to the Washington Commanders. They also signed linebacker Cam Riley in the moves. To create […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - JULY 30: Miami Dolphins quarterback Mark Gronowski (16) throws the ball during the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on July 30, 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins announced the re-signing of quarterback Mark Gronowski on Sunday, nine days after he had been waived by the team. The return comes a couple of days after Miami’s opening preseason game of the year, a 20-7 loss to the Washington Commanders. They also signed linebacker Cam Riley in the moves. To create space under the NFL’s roster limit rules, the Dolphins moved offensive lineman Jamaree Salyer to the injured reserve list and waived cornerback Ethan Robinson with an injury designation. Gronowski started his college career at South Dakota State, where he won two Football Championship Subdivision national championships and was named FCS’s top offensive player in 2023, winning the Walter Payton Award. He transferred to Iowa for the 2025 season, throwing for 1,751 yards in 13 games with 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions. His 58 combined victories at South Dakota State and Iowa is the most wins ever for a starting quarterback in NCAA history. He signed as an undrafted free agent with the Dolphins in May, then was waived on August 7. The Colts hosted Gronowski for a tryout on Saturday before he returned to South Florida. Riley joins Miami after signing as an undrafted free agent with the New England Patriots in 2025. He spent time with the Tennessee Titans practice squad last year. He began his college career at Auburn in 2020 before finishing with a one-year stint at Florida State in 2024. Salyer signed as a free agent with the Dolphins in March. He has appeared in 64 career games, starting 40 times, splitting time between left tackle and right guard. He was a 2020 sixth-round pick in 2022 coming out of Georgia. The move to IR in training camp essentially ends his season before it began. Robinson joined the Dolphins as an undrafted free agent out of Minnesota last year. He played his first three years of college at Bucknell. As a rookie with Miami, he appeared in two games playing nine special teams snaps. The Dolphins head into Preseason Week 2 with a game against the New York Giants on the schedule. Miami and New York are also scheduled to hold a joint practice on Thursday, a practice that will be open to the public as part of the Dolphins’ training camp schedule.

After stepping out of bounds prior to catching a previous Malik Willis pass, he made up for it by making an acrobatic one-handed snag. Clearly, he’s headed to the Hall of Fame. Realistically, Douglas’ mix of size and athleticism gives Miami something they’ve lacked in their receiver room. Sadly, those expectations were confirmed a short time ago. #Vikings defender Jamal Adams, who was carted off in yesterday’s preseason game, was diagnosed with a season-ending knee injury, source says. His season is over before it began. pic.twitter.com/BEOiYggDFR — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) August 16, 2026 Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network has confirmed that the non-contact injury that Adams sustained to his right knee on Saturday afternoon was a season-ending one. His chance to play a significant role in Brian Flores’ defense in 2026 is over before it really got started. The injury came on the play that saw the Giants score their lone touchdown of the afternoon, as Jaxson Dart broke out of the pocket and scrambled to his left before finding rookie Malachi Fields for a 15-yard touchdown. Adams was flowing towards the play and went down without being touched. He went to the injury tent after the play, and after that was taken back to the locker room on a cart. Adams had made a really nice tackle for loss on the previous defensive series. You hate to see something like this for a veteran like him, as from all reports he had really gotten up to speed on the defense quickly and was poised to be the sort of player that Flores could move around to different spots in the Vikings’ defensive scheme. There has not been any word yet on the injury to quarterback Max Brosmer, who was supposed to finish out the fourth quarter of yesterday’s game but was pulled after one series with an injury to his right wrist. Carson Wentz, who played most of the third quarter, went back into the game in Brosmer’s place and finished out the contest. When we get an update on that injury, we will pass that one along to you as well.

title: Minnesota Vikings News and Links: What Did You Take Away From The First Preseason Game?
summary: The first preseason game is in the books and it was nice to see the players get out there and compete against an opponent. I do not put a lot of stock into the performances at this point. After the joint practices and next week’s game, we should have a better idea. From what I […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 15: Jacob Thomas #39 of the Minnesota Vikings intercepts a pass intended for Kayvon Thibodeaux #5 of the New York Giants during the pre-season game at MetLife Stadium on August 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. From what I recall, I did notice Orange and Loudermilk getting some good penetration into the backfield a couple of times. Obviously, Myles Price looked good as did Claiborne when he can get to the edge. Jacob Thomas got the interception but I thought he showed up elsewhere as well. I am looking forward to seeing Jakobe Thomas and to see Jefferson play against someone else. I suppose he will only play in the practices vs the Ravens and not in the preseason game next week. What did you see in the game? 2026 Vikings Training Camp Full Schedule https://www.vikings.com/schedule/vikings-events/training-camp/schedule DATE : TIME : PRACTICE Monday, Aug. 17 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. Wednesday, Aug. 19 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. : Joint Practice with Baltimore Ravens Thursday, Aug. 20 : Noon – 5 p.m. : 2:30 p.m. : Joint Practice with Baltimore Ravens The Minnesota Vikings 2026 preseason schedule features three matchups Week 2: Saturday, August 22 vs. Baltimore Ravens (12:00 PM ET) Week 3: Friday, August 28 at Denver Broncos (Time TBD) Minnesota Vikings News and Links Kyler Murray Makes Vikings Debut; J.J. McCarthy Plays Most of 1st Half at Giants https://www.vikings.com/news/jj-mccarthy-kyler-murray-preseason-debut-giants-2026 Murray was 2-of-3 passing for 10 yards against the Giants with a passer rating of 71.5. “It was a blast,” he told reporters postgame. “The reality really is kind of settin’ in. I talked to my family this weekend and just, spending seven years in one spot, everything for me has been brand new this weekend — from getting on the bus with new faces to traveling in a new plane, new seat, new operation — and I’m just really embracing what’s new for me. Today was a blast, man.” … The Vikings faced third-and-4 at the Giants 17 and Murray targeted Jones, but the pass went slightly outside the RB’s grasp. Minnesota settled for a 35-yard Will Reichard field goal to take an early 3-0 lead. “I thought that first group ran it [well], and we had that third-down conversion to J.A., going down and making that nice play,” O’Connell told Vikings Entertainment Network’s Tatum Everett during a halftime interview. “Had a chance to convert on the third down and just time on task — Aaron Jones sitting down right on the chains on the check-down, Kyler might think he’s breaking out, Aaron’s sitting down. Little things that we’re going to continue to work out as we go here. “But I thought Kyler commanded the offense well; I would have loved to see that group get in the end zone,” O’Connell added. During his postgame press conference, O’Connell noted the Vikings are “doing a lot in our run game on those early downs.” “We might not have shown a lot of the things that maybe we’ve been working on, but there were still some principles of … what we want to see,” he said. “I thought the guys ran off the ball; they were physical.” Murray later echoed the coach’s comments. “Communication went well. The checks and operations went great, the o-line did their thing,” he said. “There were big, gaping holes that [the running backs] didn’t get touched until 5, 6, 7 yards down the field. That’s kind of what K.O. wanted to see, guys coming off the ball and getting the run game going. “I know I didn’t get many ops, but like I said, I’m blessed to be out there again,” Murray added. “I haven’t played since October, so I had a blast.” Murray played behind the Vikings starting five offensive line of LT Christian Darrisaw, LG Donovan Jackson, C Blake Brandel, RG Will Fries and RT Brian O’Neill. When O’Connell swapped out Murray for J.J. McCarthy, he also changed out the entire OL for the following: LT Ryan Van Demark, LG Joe Huber, C Michael Jurgens, RG Walter Rouse and RG Caleb Tiernan. McCarthy and Company played the remainder of the first half, during which he completed 4-of-7 passes for 34 yards with a 69.9 passer rating. The group struggled to find its rhythm because of offensive penalties and a Giants defense that left in many of its starters. The second-team offense went three-and-out to start, with Johnny Hekker punting for Minnesota. McCarthy’s second series started stronger, as he connected with TE Ben Yurosek for 7 yards, then handed off to rookie RB Demond Claiborne on consecutive plays. With a new set of downs, McCarthy stepped off his back foot and fired over the middle to Myles Price for a 17-yard gain; the Vikings were awarded an extra 5 when New York’s Deonte Banks was penalized for defensive holding. “[J.J.] hung in the pocket, had a little push there and was able to throw the ball in between the numbers in the intermediate part of the field, which I thought was big-time,” O’Connell said. Asked about the play, McCarthy said he saw single-high coverage and knew Price would be in a 1-on-1 situation. “Just feeling stuff beneath my feet, that’s the reps and the experience. Give it time. Trust the field beneath you,” McCarthy said. “I saw he was 1-on-1 and know he’s a ball player, so he’s going to go make that play.” Shortly thereafter, however, back-to-back penalties on Tiernan set the Vikings behind the 8-ball with 10 minutes left in the first half. McCarthy got a short pass to Price but followed with two incompletions that led to another Hekker punt. “Penalties have shot us in the foot,” O’Connell said at the half. “As we were driving there, J.J. made a nice completion and then we start going backward with penalties.” … “Little miscues here and there, getting the handoff on a jet sweep, the timing on that, on J.J.’s first play — we’ve gotta clean up that stuff,” O’Connell said. “That’s what preseason’s for, but we’re trying to win a football game here today.” O’Connell noted the upcoming joint practices with the Ravens on Wednesday and Thursday and extra opportunity that provides, as well as two more exhibition games against Baltimore and Denver. “We’ve got two great days planned versus Baltimore and then a bunch of time leading up into the season to make sure we get these guys on the same page,” he said. “What I am seeing, though, is a confident group. I think they feel like they’re gelling, they’re coming together in a way that they know what we’re trying to get done. They know the philosophy behind it. “And as we’re able to kind of fully unleash what we’re doing, we expect to see the play style hold up and really be a part of what we want to be,” O’Connell added. Following the game, McCarthy acknowledged there are “several things to clean up” and said he appreciated feeling familiarity in the system, “seeing everything clearly” and operating with several different teammates. “It was just a lot of fun being back out there playing football again,” he said. Kyler Murray’s debut, Caleb Banks’ inconsistencies, and a breakout performance Vikings preseason win vs. Giants https://atozsports.com/nfl/minnesota-vikings-news/minnesota-vikings-preseason-win-giants-kyler-murray-caleb-banks-jj-mccarthy/ EDGE 3 is reaching a crisis point We knew going into training camp that EDGE3 was going to be a big weakness on the team, and there were questions about whether or not Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins could be the guy. Earlier this week, I wrote about how Ingram-Dawkins could be a secret weapon against 13 personel, and it still holds true, but it was not a good day for him. He struggled to attack the outside shoulder of the offensive tackle, and broke contain multiple times on run plays, allowing big gains. Now, some of that…
