title: Steelers Film Room: Highs and lows of 2026 preseason debut against the Green Bay Packers
summary: Just a few days ago, the Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off their 2026 season with an impressively lopsided 28-9 victory over the Green Bay Packers. While we must acknowledge that neither team featured its star players, nor the type of playcalling we can expect once the games start to count for real, it’s also hard to […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Drew Allar #16 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates after rushing for a touchdown in the second half against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just a few days ago, the Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off their 2026 season with an impressively lopsided 28-9 victory over the Green Bay Packers. While we must acknowledge that neither team featured its star players, nor the type of playcalling we can expect once the games start to count for real, it’s also hard to introduce yourself to a new fanbase in a more impressive fashion than Mike McCarthy and his staff did on Thursday night. This is going to be quite a meaty post with several clips to share and examine, so let’s not beat around the bush. The following are highlights and lowlights of my impressions from the game. If any of these clips inspire some curiosity, or if you have any insights to add to the conversation, remember to get down in the comments section and join the conversation. Offensive line hiccups There’s going to be a lot of positives we’ll look at from this game, so let’s start off with a dose of negativity before we wash things down with what went well. The Steelers offensive line got off to a tough start on Thursday before settling in once both teams’ reserves took over. Collectively, the Steelers allowed 10 pressures and 3 sacks in pass protection. Four of those pressures were at the hands of the starting lineup — Troy Fautanu (2), Mason McCormick (1), and Dylan Cook (1) — and a fifth pressure was credited to running back Travis Homer, who started the game with both Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle in street clothes for this game. The rushing attack managed just 2.7 yards per carry. And Fautanu was tagged for both a false start penalty and an offensive holding call. It certainly wasn’t a pristine showing for the unit. If you’re looking for reasons to soften that showing, there are explanations/excuses that could be made. For starters, the 10 pressures sound worse than it was because on a couple of plays, multiple pressures were allowed, meaning it wasn’t 10 plays that resulted in pressure, just a few really bad snaps. There is also the bit about Fautanu, McCormick, and Cook all flipping to the opposite side from where they played in 2025. A few bumps and bruises were to be expected. And perhaps most important to remember each year: this was the first preseason game of the year. Preseason games exist to ramp up for the season physically and to iron out mental mistakes. The Steelers by no means should be satisfied with this performance, but these issues will matter much more if they linger into the first month of the season. Still, it’s better to make these mistakes now while there is still time to adjust. Here are the three sacks Pittsburgh allowed in the game: Sack allowed on first drive of Steelers v Packers pic.twitter.com/xsL5iT6pU9 — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) August 14, 2026 This first sack is a comedy of errors, a true team sack. Fautanu and Homer are the two main culprits on the play, but aren’t all that goes wrong here. We’ll start with Fautanu, who isn’t able to get deep enough quickly enough. His defender is out wide of tight end Darnell Washington, who himself is running a route. Fautaun kicks off, but doesn’t get enough depth for how wide and fast the Packers edge player is. Fautanu’s hips flip to the point that his outside hip is parallel with the quarterback, never a good sign. He doesn’t have enough power from this position to fully displace the pass rusher off his path to the quarterback, but to Fautanu’s credit, he is able to widen the rush enough that Mason Rudolph had a chance to climb and slide out to his left if there hadn’t also been other failures in the Steelers’ pass protection. Homer is the second biggest culprit on this play. He isn’t in a good base when he meets the blitzing linebacker and is immediately rocked back onto his heels. Unfortunately, he gets driven back at the exact moment that Rudolph tries to climb the pocket, and Homer ends up right in his quarterback’s lap. This sends Homer further off balance and causes Rudolph to pull the ball down and awkwardly try to shuffle his feet with no space to move. This is only worsened when a Packer (55) coming on a delayed stunt violently throws himself into this cluster, causing Rudolph to further stumble and lose all chance of regaining his feet to reset his throw. I’m not positive of their blocking assignments, so I won’t critique either of the guards here, but I will note that the stunting Packer (55) goes unpicked up. Intuitively, I would assume Spencer Anderson (74) would have been the best to pick that up, be he first double-teams a defender with Zach Fraizer, and then picks up the defender who initially engaged with McCormick before countering inside. Likewise, I won’t be critical of Rudolph here because I don’t know how he’s coached to go through his progressions on this play. Watching it in the All-22 view, it seems obvious that Germie Bernard gets open fairly quickly in the middle, right in the space vacated by the blitzing linebackers, but Rudolph appears to be reading the left side of the field first on this play. That could be what the play called for, and the pass blocking by Homer speeds his process up and makes the pocket messy quickly. Just a bad play that I’m sure will be discussed in this week’s meetings. 2nd sack of the game. This one is squarely on 60. Lets 57 get a long arm to his chest and can't do anything but try to swipe the arm down. Unfortunately, he's giving ground and loses balance at the end, and falls back on his heels. The defender keeps his feet to finish the sack pic.twitter.com/daGG1r9Wo8 — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) August 14, 2026 Sack number two isn’t too complicated. Cook simple gets beat here. The routes are too long developing to get away with how quickly Cook gives this pressure up. Again, the two players who maybe are open enough to try a quick throw — Homer in the flat and Roman Wilson running a hook route that would definitely have been contested — were on the opposite side of the field from where Rudolph’s progression starts, so it’s hard to pin this on the quarterback without knowing exactly what was called. The Steelers did have the numbers advantage on the right half of the field, so it makes sense that Rudolph’s eyes were there. Pretty diabolical look from GB against a young QB. Put 8 on LOS and end up dropping 3. Idk the assignment, but I don't love 27 getting a free rush, especially since I don't think 77 needed to help with 47. Think 16 has the velo to get this throw off, but 18 was right to hold this pic.twitter.com/PxqmeeiD2F — Ryan Parish (@ArmchairScout21) August 14, 2026 The final sack of the game feels like some sort of communication bust. Watching it live, it was easy to blame Broderick Jones for this one. Again, without knowing the exact blocking assignments on the play, it’s tough to speak definitively, but you never like to see a free rusher come screaming off the edge virtually untouched. Was this Howard failing to identify that rusher as a hot read? Was this Jones misunderstanding his assignment? He goes to help guard Brock Hoffman on a double team that doesn’t look necessary on tape, but the Packers front could have led to some of the confusion. Green Bay placed eight defenders on the line of scrimmage with two linebackers lining up in a double mug look — one on each shoulder of the center — and the Steelers might have believed there would be some stunts Jones would need to help with and that the defensive back on the edge was bluffing. Howard seemed ready to roll to his right quickly, so it’s possible this was also part of their design, but if so, I don’t like that there was only one route runner running to that side of the field, and in a concept that would have them trailing well behind the…

title: Mike McCarthy says Steelers saw Drew Allar as a first-round talent
summary: In a game where Pittsburgh Steelers fans hoped to gain some clarity on who would gain some ground and take the backup quarterback job in a battle between Mason Rudolph and Will Howard, it was the third-round developmental rookie quarterback, Drew Allar, who stole the show. The 76th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 13: Drew Allar #16 talks with head coach Mike McCarthy of the Pittsburgh Steelers during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Acrisure Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images In a game where Pittsburgh Steelers fans hoped to gain some clarity on who would gain some ground and take the backup quarterback job in a battle between Mason Rudolph and Will Howard, it was the third-round developmental rookie quarterback, Drew Allar, who stole the show. The 76th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft went 10-of-13 passing with two passing touchdowns and a rushing touchdown. Appearing on The Pat McAfee Show,Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy revealed that the Steelers were not only high on Allar as a prospect, but they believed that he was a first-round talent. “When we drafted Drew, we felt like we were getting a first-round pick,” McCarthy said. “When you know just the value that our personnel department had on him, you know, coming out of his junior year, and just, you would sit there and listen to all the reports and just, as you talk about the timeline of his career, what happened this senior, he had the injury, and so forth, so, and all that’s holding true.” "When we drafted Drew Allar we felt like we were getting a first round pick.. All of that is holding true" ~ Coach McCarthy #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/MN1n2icwEj — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) August 14, 2026 Once upon a time, Allar was considered a first-round caliber prospect by the NFL Draft community. His 6-foot-5 frame, combined with serious arm talent, gave scouts reason to believe he was worthy of a top selection after his junior season. It seems like the Steelers head coach was thinking these same things about Allar. McCarthy seems to be thrilled that he had the opportunity to select Allar in the third round this past April. While he stole the show in the first preseason game, there is still plenty to learn for Allar, who is having his footwork and throwing mechanics refined under McCarthy. We saw plenty of the early returns from the coaching the Steelers head coach has done on the young quarterback in his NFL debut. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Seahawks work out former Oregon State star running back
summary: The Seattle Seahawks enter the second week of preseason with a tryout for yet another running back, one who should be familiar to college football fans in the Pacific Northwest. Former Oregon State star Anthony Hankerson, who was one of the few bright spots on an otherwise brutal Beavers team, worked out with the Seahawks […]
full_text: CORVALLIS, OR - NOVEMBER 08: Oregon State Beavers running back Anthony Hankerson (0) reacts after scoring a touchdown during a college football game between the Oregon State Beavers and Sam Houston Bearkats on November 8, 2025, at Reser Stadium in Corvallis, Oregon.(Photo by Brian Murphy/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks enter the second week of preseason with a tryout for yet another running back, one who should be familiar to college football fans in the Pacific Northwest. Former Oregon State star Anthony Hankerson, who was one of the few bright spots on an otherwise brutal Beavers team, worked out with the Seahawks over the weekend, per the NFL’s transaction wire. Hankerson was recently let go by the Miami Dolphins, who signed him as an undrafted free agent. Originally a member of the Colorado Buffaloes, Hankerson transferred to Oregon State in 2024 and became the first Beavers running back since Jacquizz Rodgers to record back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons. As an extra bit of trivia, Hankerson was the main Oregon State replacement for former Seahawks draft pick Damien Martinez, who’s currently on the Green Bay Packers roster. Hankerson, who had a Pro Day but didn’t participate in the NFL Scouting Combine, did receive a minicamp invite from the Seahawks after the draft before signing with Miami. Seattle’s running back room is considerably banged up, with neither Jadarian Price nor Emanuel Wilson featuring against the Dallas Cowboys due to their respective injuries. Jacardia Wright has also been dealing with a leg injury and sat out the preseason opener, leaving George Holani, Velus Jones Jr, T.J. Harden, and Justin Jones as the available backs on the night. It remains to be seen how soon any of Price, Wilson, or Wright will be able to return for this week’s joint practice and subsequent game against the Tennessee Titans. At this point, Hankerson is highly likely to be camp/preseason fodder just to get through the rest of August, with the chance to impress enough for practice squad consideration. We’ll see if the Seahawks sign him ahead of Monday’s practice.

title: A Seattle Seahawks 53-man roster projection after Week 1 of preseason
summary: The Seattle Seahawks have completed their first week of preseason, which definitely didn’t go as well as hoped. While preseason final scores mean not a jot, individual and collective performances for players looking to solidify roster spots do mean something, and the Seahawks’ reserve largely struggled in Saturday’s 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. After […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Mike Morris #94 of the Seattle Seahawks gets set during the first quarter of the NFL preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks have completed their first week of preseason, which definitely didn’t go as well as hoped. While preseason final scores mean not a jot, individual and collective performances for players looking to solidify roster spots do mean something, and the Seahawks’ reserve largely struggled in Saturday’s 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys . After every preseason game, we’ll be doing an updated roster projection. This is, of course, an initial 53-man roster and not remotely close to what the roster will look like over the course of the season. Heck, this projection might be obsolete by Tuesday, but you know what? Offense (26) Quarterback (3): Sam Darnold, Drew Lock, Jalen Milroe Cut: N/A Notes : If you think Milroe played himself off the team last night I think you’re being a bit too hasty. If he looks underwhelming for the rest of preseason then maybe a conversation can be had. Running Back (3): Jadarian Price (R), Emanuel Wilson, George Holani Cut: Jacardia Wright, T.J. Harden, Justin Jones (R), Velus Jones Jr PUP: Zach Charbonnet Notes : There’s no need to keep four running backs for a month if/when Zach Charbonnet is back in October. Just elevate a practice squad back if necessary and you’re fine. Price, Wilson, and Holani are clearly the top three and there’s some distance between them and the rest. Fullback (1): Brady Russell Cut: Brock Lampe IR: Robbie Ouzts Notes : This is going to be complicated. Brock Lampe played only three snaps in the Cowboys game but unlike Russell, he’s a true fullback. Russell is more of a FB/TE hybrid whose real value is on special teams. My feeling is that Lampe could be a practice squad stash as a late arrival to the team. Wide Receiver (6): Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Cooper Kupp, Rashid Shaheed, Tory Horton, Jake Bobo , Montorie Foster Cut: Emmanuel Henderson Jr (R), Cody White, Ricky White III, Irv Charles, Rashad Rochelle Notes : This is not a spur of the moment thing from the preseason game; Foster has had a strong summer and the most telling aspect of the Cowboys game was how he was getting second-team run over Ricky White III. Cody White has cleared waivers a million times before, so it’s reasonable to think that the Seahawks could roster Foster through cutdown day and Cody (and Ricky) are on the practice squad. Tight End (3): A.J. Barner, Elijah Arroyo, Eric Saubert Cut: Nick Kallerup, Nick Vannett Notes : I think we should put Kallerup’s rookie season in perspective. He did not play a single snap through Week 8, at which point Eric Saubert had to go on IR and Kallerup got some extended playing time. Elijah Arroyo suffered his own injury during the Atlanta Falcons game and Kallerup played 29 snaps. Once Saubert returned, Kallerup’s snap count dipped and he was a healthy Super Bowl scratch. He doesn’t even play much on special teams. As long as the three guys ahead of him are healthy, I think Seattle is more willing to risk him on waivers this go-round. Offensive Line (10) : Charles Cross, Abe Lucas, Josh Jones, Mason Richman, Anthony Bradford, Olu Oluwatimi, Jalen Sundell, Grey Zabel, Christian Haynes , Beau Stephens (R) Cut: Federico Maranges, Bobby Hart , Amari Kight, Logan Brown, Bryce Cabeldue Notes : Now that I’ve been to training camp for a week and watched the first Seahawks preseason game, I think Christian Haynes is closer to safe than cut. Beau Stephens has been mostly with the third-team and ain’t challenging Anthony Bradford any time soon. Bobby Hart, Amari Kight, and Logan Brown all but annihilated their roster chances in the span of a few hours. Cabeldue having all of his snaps come deep into the game is telling for his future. Mason Richman I think is in good position as a G/C. Defense (24) Defensive Line (5): Byron Murphy II, Leonard Williams, Jarran Reed, Rylie Mills, Mike Morris Cut: J.R. Singleton, Bubba Thomas , Brandon Pili , Uso Seumalo (R) , Deven Eastern (R) Notes : Much like last year, if the Seahawks want to keep a true nose tackle instead of just playing Byron Murphy II or Jarran Reed there all the time— notice that Reed is now listed as a DE in the depth chart —I guess they could have Pili on the active roster again. Otherwise, just do the usual practice squad elevation and determine from there whether elevations turn into a promotion to the 53. Outside Linebacker (4): Derick Hall, Uchenna Nwosu , Dante Fowler Jr, DeMarcus Lawrence Cut: Jared Ivey, Connor O’Toole , Marvin Jones Jr (R), Jamie Sheriff, Jalan Gaines , Aidan Hubbard (R) Notes : A week at training camp was discouraging enough for me when assessing the bottom part of the depth chart. The first preseason game only affirmed my fears that, outside of Jalan Gaines, there’s nothing happening here. Any fifth pure EDGE on this team is stashed for special teams only. Seattle will either make a trade or just have Morris be the emergency fifth option. Inside Linebacker (4): Ernest Jones IV, Drake Thomas, Tyrice Knight, Patrick O’Connell Cut: Chazz Surratt, Chris Paul Jr, Aaron Smith Notes : The fourth spot comes down to O’Connell or Surratt, and whichever player is waived is a practice squad signing. Surratt likely has higher special teams value but that’s about it. Cornerback (6): Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe, Nehemiah Pritchett , Julian Neal (R), Terrion Arnold, Noah Igbinoghene Cut: Shemar Jean-Charles, Jordan Washington (R), Michael Dansby (R), Andre Fuller (R) Notes : Let’s assume Arnold is on the roster and not suspended for Week 1. Neal is seemingly closer to practicing again so I don’t think he’s an IR candidate. The Seahawks may keep six corners and kind of figure it out with playing time for anyone not named Witherspoon or Jobe. Safety (5): Julian Love, Ty Okada, Nick Emmanwori, Bud Clark (R), A.J. Finley Cut: Maxen Hook, Rodney Thomas II, D’Anthony Bell Notes : One of the fascinating developments is seeing A.J. Finley take the primary second-team safety snaps alongside Bud Clark. D’Anthony Bell’s big nickel role may not be needed that much if Emmanwori is a full go come Week 1. Rodney Thomas II didn’t play any snaps until the second half, which was generally the third-team defense. This is still a very tense competition for fifth safety, but I think Finley is really making a push to stay on the 53. Special Teams (3) Kicker (1) : Jason Myers Punter (1) : Michael Dickson Long Snapper (1) : Chris Stoll Cut: No one Notes : Nothing to debate here. We go again next Monday after the Tennessee Titans exhibition!

title: Devon Witherspoon is latest Seahawk from Russell Wilson trade to cash in
summary: The Seattle Seahawks took care of one of their superstars, making Devon Witherspoon the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history following his $132 million extension. Perhaps this distinction will last about five seconds once Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots figure something out, but who cares? ’Spoon got paid, and the Seahawks have a true […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 8: Devon Witherspoon #21 of the Seattle Seahawks reacts after a play during the second quarter of the NFL Super Bowl LX football game against the New England Patriots, at Levi's Stadium on February 8, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks took care of one of their superstars, making Devon Witherspoon the highest-paid cornerback in NFL history following his $132 million extension . Perhaps this distinction will last about five seconds once Christian Gonzalez and the New England Patriots figure something out, but who cares? ’Spoon got paid, and the Seahawks have a true franchise corner for the first time since Richard Sherman. Of course, you can’t tell the story of Witherspoon’s arrival in Seattle without tying it directly to the Russell Wilson trade. In some respects, while Wilson’s playing days are over , the effects of the trade are still not finished yet. We’re four years removed from the seismic, franchise-altering day when the Seahawks sent Wilson to the Denver Broncos for a treasure trove of draft picks (not to mention current backup quarterback, Drew Lock). Charles Cross (No. 9 overall, 2022) The first foundational piece of the Wilson deal—yes, it’s ironic given the struggles on the OL and questionable investments when Russ was QB— Cross agreed to a four-year contract extension worth $104.4 million . He became the first first-round pick by John Schneider to get an extension since Earl Thomas. Cross has shown himself to be at least an above-average left tackle, with room to grow to become one of the NFL’s best. Add in the extension right tackle Abe Lucas received before last season started , and the Seahawks have good continuity at both tackle spots. Devon Witherspoon (No. 5, 2023) The Seahawks taking a cornerback early? They never do that! Well, in Pete Carroll’s final season, that’s what happened. While all outside eyes were on Seattle getting Jalen Carter (perhaps, in part, because none of the quarterback options fell Seattle’s way), the Seahawks were wowed by ‘Spoon and spent a top-five pick on a cornerback for the first time since Shawn Springs. All ‘Spoon has done is make three Pro Bowls and earn second-team All-Pro honors in Seattle’s Super Bowl season. He may not have the gaudy interception stats but he’s proven to be one of those “force multipliers” who can cover, tackle in run support, and blitz quarterbacks into pure panic and misery. As already mentioned, there are 132 million reasons to be thankful that the Broncos cratered in 2022 and put Seattle in position to get Witherspoon. Derick Hall (No. 37 overall, 2023) The final piece of the Russell Wilson trade as a 2023 second-round pick, Hall just landed a three-year, $42 million extension that is comparatively modest in the current edge rusher market. He played much better than the two regular season sacks showed, and his Super Bowl performance was arguably game MVP worthy. Seattle is banking on Hall turning it up a notch and really upping his sack productivity, especially with DeMarcus Lawrence retiring and Uchenna Nwosu set to hit free agency. Honorable mention: Boye Mafe (No. 40, 2022) The Seahawks did not pay Boye Mafe in free agency, although it wasn’t like he was a draft bust. Mafe agreed to a three-year, $60 million contract with the pass rush starved Cincinnati Bengals . While Mafe didn’t have a great contract year, he still racked up nine sacks in 2023 and another six in 2024. Just within the 2026 calendar year, Messrs Cross, Hall, Witherspoon, and Mafe have combined for $338.4 million in new contracts, whether through a Seahawks contract extension or free agent money. This is not to even include the knock-on effect of the Seahawks having that draft capital freedom to get Jaxon Smith-Njigba ( highest paid receiver in NFL history ), Kenneth Walker III ( biggest free agent RB contract in NFL history ), and Zach Charbonnet (TBD on his future) with their native picks. The only player directly drafted by the Seahawks in the Wilson trade not to pan out was Tyreke Smith, a 2022 fifth-round selection who never really managed to get going as an edge rusher. I don’t think anyone is losing sleep because Tyreke Smith didn’t turn into a serviceable NFL rotational man. It’s easy to say the Seahawks generally stuck to the consensus board and didn’t overthink it at the top of their recent drafts, but front office competence, player development, and a positive team culture all matter. If merely having the draft capital could build a contender then the Cleveland Browns should’ve had more than one playoff win this century. The Wilson trade might have been both encouraging and wobbly in the early years when the Seahawks were in the same “treading water” position that generally defined much of the back-end of the Wilson era. Not having a definitive franchise quarterback didn’t help matters, either. But the combination of continued smart drafting, sound roster building, a shrewd free agent signing to get that potential franchise quarterback , and a home run hire at head coach has quickly turned the Seahawks into a championship force when it could’ve been just as easy to fall into the abyss. Seattle cashed out on Russ at the right time, struck gold in the draft, and now their core players from that trade have cashed in.

title: 49ers News: Can’t wait to see Kittle back
summary: Tight end Jake Tonges, a former tech bro, on ‘full-circle moment’ after $8 million contract with 49ers (paywall)“The 49ers run a lot of 22-personnel formations, or in other words, sets with two tight ends. On paper, Tonges is a prototypical receiving tight end and Farrell is known for his blocking. First-year tight ends coach Cam […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - AUGUST 13: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers walks on the field before a preseason NFL game against the Tennessee Titans on August 13, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tight end Jake Tonges, a former tech bro, on ‘full-circle moment’ after $8 million contract with 49ers (paywall) “The 49ers run a lot of 22-personnel formations, or in other words, sets with two tight ends. On paper, Tonges is a prototypical receiving tight end and Farrell is known for his blocking. First-year tight ends coach Cam Clemmons has tried to help them out of those boxes. Clemmons, previously an assistant offensive line coach for the 49ers, has been especially helpful to Tonges. “That’s been my challenge to him, is, Jake, your ceiling isn’t last year,” Clemmons said. “Last year was just kind of the beginning.” Key 49ers position battle remains undecided heading into preseason Week 2 “Wide receiver Jacob Cowing had a couple of hard falls during practice, the second of which resulted in a diving reception on a deep pass from Purdy. Cowing had a couple of steps on cornerback Deommodore Lenoir, and he laid out to catch the 45-yard downfield throw. Earlier, Cowing and Marques Sigle took hard spills after they both went up for a Purdy pass along the left side of the field.“ 49ers’ George Kittle eyes return to practice, opener in Australia “For most of the process, Kittle said he has had to focus on doing as many seated and standing calf raises as possible every day. His workouts, however, have taken on a more football-specific approach of late. As the Niners practiced last week, Kittle was running and cutting at nearly full speed while running routes and catching passes from a team staffer on a side field. On Sunday, Kittle said he’s hitting the speed benchmarks set for him on the GPS and is “pretty close” to hitting the same speed numbers he hit before the injury. Kittle said he has a target date in mind for returning to practice but declined to share it. He added that he’s “very confident” he won’t start the season on the physically unable to perform list, meaning he intends to be back within the season’s first four games.“ 49ers OC Klay Kubiak shares updates on Rourke, Stribling, Evans, Kittle, and Purdy “”There’s a time and a place, but you want the mindset to drive the football, and Brock has both tools, and Brock is exceptional at whatever layering it is. Throwing it over, zoning defenders, finding holes in the defense, he’s exceptional at that. But you want the mindset as a quarterback, ‘I’m driving the football.’ We remind him of that, and he has both tools. So, I think the nickname’s funny, I appreciate it, but it’s cool that Brock kind of takes it personally, too, and says, ‘No, I’m going to drive the ball. I’m not going to layer things.’ But you got to have both tools in your bag. So, it’s kind of a funny deal between him and Raheem.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 13 of 49ers Camp: Mike Evans Dominates (Finally) “He still doesn’t create a ton of separation against man coverage, but neither does Evans. Both receivers are excellent at catching passes over the heads of defensive backs. And Stribling in particular is fearless when it comes to running full speed across the field. It looks like he’s being groomed to start this season, considering he’s not playing any special teams. As opposed to Deebo Samuel, who’s a punt returner and a kick returner. And when he plays with the starters, he mostly is a running back.” 49ers 53-man roster projection (paywall) “The 49ers probably have to keep five, and if we’re talking about the best 53, all seven of these players should make the team. James Thompson Jr. has an abundance of untapped upside, but he’s not polished. Valdez has certainly done enough to earn a spot, but he’s not consistent. Eason, meanwhile, is an imperious force who can hold up against double teams. He’s a Day 1 NFL-caliber player. Everyone else is a no-brainer.“ George Kittle expects to return to the 49ers ‘sooner than later’ “I’ve been running around a lot. Hitting top speeds. Hopefully, we’re back in pads practicing sooner than later. Just trying to check the boxes and not be a dumbass is what I would say. Kittle said he spoke with Richard Sherman about the rehab process of an Achilles injury. He said building a strong foundation after the next eight weeks is the most important part: “If you build a strong foundation, get your calf muscle back, get your strength back, then you’re allowed to train faster and get your body ready to go faster. So, we dominated those 8 weeks. Had a really good rehab.” Kittle mentioned how a Week 1 target date made it easy to light a fire under him. He said he was doing seated calf raises within ten minutes of taking his cast off. Kittle said he’s hitting the numbers that he needs to hit as far as the GPS times and markers go. Kittle understands that he needs to practice before he plays: “I don’t want my first time in pads traveling to Australia. I don’t think that’d be a very smart idea. These next couple of weeks are everything. That’ll let me know whether I’m able to play Week 1 or not.”

title: George Kittle expects to return to the 49ers ‘sooner than later’
summary: The San Francisco 49ers returned to practice on Sunday. A couple of players sat out, beyond the usual suspects. Gracen Halton (ankle) and Dominick Puni (concussion) missed practice. We’ll see if those injuries prevent Halton and Puni from participating in this week’s joint practice or preseason game against the Chargers. As for quarterback Kurtis Rourke […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - JUNE 03: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers speaks with the media after a team OTA practice at SAP Performance Facility on June 3, 2026 in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers returned to practice on Sunday. A couple of players sat out, beyond the usual suspects. Gracen Halton (ankle) and Dominick Puni (concussion) missed practice. We’ll see if those injuries prevent Halton and Puni from participating in this week’s joint practice or preseason game against the Chargers. As for quarterback Kurtis Rourke and his rib injury, offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak doesn’t believe his injury will be long-term: “I don’t think it’ll be long. I think he just needs to heal up a little bit and get him back out there. We don’t think it’s anything long-term.” Rourke did not practice during the previous two practices. Kubiak said Rourke was “excellent” as far as getting the huddle organized and getting the play call in, and executed “really well,” saying he was “really pleased with how he played.” You have to remember, it was Rourke’s first live action since 2024. When asked if he had seen enough if he had seen enough for Rourke to stick around in the NFL, Kubiak said it’s “premature,” despite Rourke having a “bright future” with a lot of room to grow: “That is why we drafted him, because he thought he was an NFL quarterback. I think we saw a lot of talent where he thought he was better than a 7th-round pick, but he had an injury in college that we knew he wasn’t going to be able to play his first year very much, so his draft value fell a little bit. But, evaluating, we saw an NFL thrower who was very bright, had the right size, and had a chance to be a player. We still think he is. I think he’s taken steps in that direction. But he’s got to keep going.” It’s one game, but Rourke made a strong statement to make the roster. As for George Kittle, Kubiak said he’s heard “relentless positivity.” Week 1 still isn’t off the table for Kittle, who seems to be trending in the right direction. Kittle spoke to the media after Sunday’s practice. The team is 17 days away from flying to Australia. He believes he “has a chance” to play. “I’ve been running around a lot. Hitting top speeds. Hopefully, we’re back in pads practicing sooner than later. Just trying to check the boxes and not be a dumbass is what I would say. Kittle said he spoke with Richard Sherman about the rehab process of an Achilles injury. He said building a strong foundation after the next eight weeks is the most important part: “If you build a strong foundation, get your calf muscle back, get your strength back, then you’re allowed to train faster and get your body ready to go faster. So, we dominated those 8 weeks. Had a really good rehab.” Kittle mentioned how a Week 1 target date made it easy to light a fire under him. He said he was doing seated calf raises within ten minutes of taking his cast off. Kittle said he’s hitting the numbers that he needs to hit as far as the GPS times and markers go. Kittle understands that he needs to practice before he plays: “I don’t want my first time in pads traveling to Australia. I don’t think that’d be a very smart idea. These next couple of weeks are everything. That’ll let me know whether I’m able to play Week 1 or not.” He added that if he’s not on the plane to Australia, then he’s staying back and rehabbing. Kittle currently weighs 245 pounds. He said he’s been playing around 242 pounds ever since his second season. He said he feels “very skinny” if he’s under 240 pounds and that he can’t block people. Kittle said playing Week 1 is still his goal, and he’ll adjust as needed. Kittle is “very confident” that he won’t begin the season on the PUP list and miss the first four games. He ended his presser saying, “sooner than later.”

title: 49ers News: Mike Evans practices again
summary: Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling?“The team has long shied away from plugging any of its young wideouts into one position, instead asking them to learn all three spots (F, X or Z) before deciding where to put them. That workload can faze some players, but coaches and teammates have said Stribling […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 13: Romello Height #94 of the San Francisco 49ers rushes pass Dan Moore Jr. #75 of the Tennessee Titans in the first half at Levi's Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling? “The team has long shied away from plugging any of its young wideouts into one position, instead asking them to learn all three spots (F, X or Z) before deciding where to put them. That workload can faze some players, but coaches and teammates have said Stribling isn’t bothered. The strong impression he left on the team was a result of the routine Stribling developed after the offseason program. Along with the studying film each day, he would say every playcall out loud or have someone recite it to him. Then, he would write it down or draw the play out so he could visualize it. Stribling would go through the playbook repeatedly, occasionally asking his mother or his girlfriend to quiz him or call out plays. He even joined fellow wideout Jordan Watkins for throwing sessions with Purdy and Jones in Nashville prior to training camp.” The Good and Not So Good from Day 12 of 49ers Camp: The Purdy-Evans Connection Needs Work “Give Samuel credit — he’s in the best shape possible and he shows every day, as opposed to lots of other veterans on the team. He’s one of the iron mans of camp so far, which is incredible….[Jack Jones] injured his hand early on Thursday night against the Titans, but practiced today and recovered a fumble. He takes the ball away from the offense seemingly every other practice, but his coverage isn’t exactly sticky. He’s an enigma. Mike Evans returns to 49ers practice as left guard competition heats up “Wide receiver Jacob Cowing, out since Aug. 5 with a hip flexor injury, returned to practice. He took a handoff on a running play, then dropped a pass from Jones. Later, he made a very nice grab of a Jones pass along the right sideline.” 49ers DC Raheem Morris evaluates young players after preseason opener “San Francisco 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris spoke with reporters after Saturday’s training camp practice. Here’s everything he had to say.” 49ers’ Gracen Halton making an impression with both burst and outburst at camp (paywall) “ After Halton’s first win in one-on-one drills earlier this month, 49ers tackle Trent Williams strolled over to the defensive line’s section to offer a handshake and encouragement. Both are Oklahoma products who met three years ago when Williams was on the sideline for a Sooners game, though Halton doubts the veteran tackle remembers the encounter. “I was one of the guys that said what’s up to him,” Halton said. “I was dang starstruck.” …Halton feels he’s making up for lost time. He hyperextended his knee on the first day of training camp and missed the initial week of practice. He didn’t exactly ease his way back into the mix when he returned, making plays in both one-on-one and 11-on-11 situations and letting everyone know about it. “That’s what I like to do,” he said. “I imagine myself as a lion going out to get the gazelle. So when I do those one-on-ones, my mindset is, I’m going off to hunt.” 49ers change up their left guard rotation; Mike Evans and Jacob Cowing return “After Thursday’s game, Kyle Shanahan said this about Jones: “We felt he fit into our scheme and was a guy that we were able to get that we think can compete for that starting job, and if not, he can have some good depth for us.” That almost sounds like they want Willis or Colby to be the guy for the job. In the same breath, this shouldn’t be viewed as a demotion for Jones, who played in his first live game since 2024 fewer than 48 hours ago. The team has to manage Jones’ inevitable soreness. After practice, Trent Williams said it’s a three-man race and “may the best man win.” He believes Willis has a “high ceiling and a lot of potential.”

full_text: Commanders center Nick Allegretti has been out since the first training camp practice dealing with a calf strain . While he has been active in walk-throughs, the injury has prevented him from full-speed work. Allegretti’s finally ready to return to practice, head coach Dan Quinn said Sunday during a virtual press conference. While there will be a ramp-up period, Allegretti will be back at practice on Tuesday when Washington gets back at it. Tight end John Bates, who has been dealing with a hamstring strain , will also start practicing with the team on Tuesday. Cornerback Trey Amos is not ready for on-field work after suffering an ankle injury shortly after being activated off the physically unable to perform list. He started camp with that designation, while recovering from a fractured fibula in 2025 and some soft-tissue soreness that accompanied his rehab. Amos got hurt once he was back to work, and it has resulted in a longer absence. “He’s continuing the rehab on his ankle,” Quinn said. “He’s dealing with soreness – it’s not like a reaggravation of the injury – but he’s not there yet in terms of being fully back and going on it. It’ll be the same schedule. You’ll see him out doing stuff while working on the side, but he won’t be fully able to participate this week.” Amos simply hasn’t practiced much at all, missing the offseason program and all but one camp practice. That’s of concern to the Commanders, who need their top cornerback available for Week 1. “I’m excited for him to get back to practicing,” Quinn said. “We all need it. That’s an important piece for Trey, too, …the movements, the skills, the conditioning. There’s certainly concern. He’s working hard, but with these next two-and-a-half weeks, those will be important to see the progress of ramping up hard, almost there and into that spot. Maybe in a week or so’s time, I’ll be able to have a better estimate.” Running back Jeremy McNichols is dealing with a quadriceps issue that will keep him out for a few weeks. That will increase opportunities for Robert Henry Jr. and Kaytron Allen, who played well in the preseason opener. Update: Washington worked out 8 players today. Dan Quinn didn’t provide an update on DT Tim Settle who’s dealing with a calf strain. Quinn today said Jeremy McNichols would be out several weeks with a quad injury. title: Commanders injury news: Marcus Mariota suffers sprained knee
summary: Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota played just four snaps during Friday’s preseason opener versus Miami. The veteran didn’t get a quick hook. He got hurt on the first offensive drive.   Mariota suffered a right MCL sprain in Washington’s 20-7 victory over the Dolphins at Northwest Stadium.  Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that fact in a […]
full_text: Commanders quarterback Marcus Mariota played just four snaps during Friday’s preseason opener versus Miami. The veteran didn’t get a quick hook. He got hurt on the first offensive drive. Mariota suffered a right MCL sprain in Washington’s 20-7 victory over the Dolphins at Northwest Stadium. Head coach Dan Quinn confirmed that fact in a Sunday press conference . Quinn said that Mariota is expected to miss the rest of the preseason, but there’s optimism he’ll be back for the start of the regular season. All things considered, that’s a positive outcome for the Commanders. They could get their No. 2 quarterback back before games that count. Quinn also said he doesn’t anticipate the Commanders bringing in another quarterback, instead handing reserves Sam Hartman and Athan Kaliakmanis more practice and preseason game reps. Mariota got hit hard on an explosive, 22-yard pass completed to Dyami Brown during Friday’s game, and came up lame after a handoff on the next play. Good to have ya back, @deuce2_ 📺 #MIAvsWAS @wusa9 pic.twitter.com/PUhHgsMJXN — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 14, 2026 Mariota was treated on the field and then in the blue medical tent before eventually leaving for the locker room with a trainer. Marcus Mariota is headed back to the locker room with assistant head athletic trainer Mark McCracken. pic.twitter.com/mlwVDhnkWT — Nicki Jhabvala (@NickiJhabvala) August 14, 2026 Mariota walked off the field without a clear limp or support from another person. He obviously did not return to a game that didn’t count, especially with his immense value backing up starter Jayden Daniels. Mariota has been called into action 14 times under Daniels , including 11 games and eight starts in 2025.

title: Commanders News: “Braves on the warpath” returns to Washington fight song
summary: The Daily Slop – 16 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. full_text: The Daily Slop – 16 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles The Athletic (paywall) What we learned from the Commanders’ preseason win over the Dolphins The Commanders’ defensive line featured all reserves, but Sonny Styles and Leo Chenal started at linebacker, and the secondary included safeties Will Harris and Quan Martin, along with veteran corner Rasul Douglas. That they couldn’t stop a Miami team lacking in playmakers and depth was alarming, but Washington quickly regrouped. After their opening score (a one-yard run by De’Von Achane), the Dolphins never made it past Washington’s 45-yard line and ended their subsequent drives with a turnover on downs, an interception, six consecutive punts and two interceptions. [Quan] Martin’s place on the roster remains uncertain, despite starting 32 of the Commanders’ last 34 games. Last season, he had a 154.6 passer rating against, the fourth-highest among NFL defenders with at least 200 coverage snaps. He also missed 15 tackles, the second-most on the Commanders behind Frankie Luvu’s 21. Martin was benched in the team’s Week 11 loss to the Dolphins in Madrid, and logged only six defensive snaps in the team’s season-ending loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Washington signed veteran safety Nick Cross as a free agent in March and has another year with Will Harris. Tyler Owens and Percy Butler are also back and, like Reaves, have been core special-teamers for Washington. To say Martin needed a strong showing on Friday would be an understatement. He delivered with a body-slamming tackle of Achane during Miami’s first drive, then the interception early in the second quarter. Also: [O]n Friday, the team not so subtly restored one piece of Native-adjacent imagery by restoring the line “Braves on a warpath” to its fight song. The line had been replaced with “Fight for our Commanders” after the name change. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE NFL.com 2026 NFL Preseason, Week 1: What We Learned from Friday’s games Commanders have battle for final RB spot(s). Jacory Croskey-Merritt and Rachaad White reside at the top of Washington’s running back depth chart. Behind them are two veterans, Jeremy McNichols and Jerome Ford, and two rookies: sixth-rounder Kaytron Allen and undrafted free agent Robert Henry Jr. Both first-year players scored on Friday, perhaps making a push for the final 53-man roster. The more impressive of the two was Henry. He had the juice, breaking off a 15-yard run early and later beating everyone to the outside for a 22-yard score . He finished with 75 yards on 12 carries (6.3 YPC). Allen also represented himself well (23 carries for 85 yards), sporting a long of 16 and taking a goal-line plunge to find the end zone. Could either or both supplant a vet on the roster? Croskey-Merrit, a 2025 seventh-rounder, shot up the depth chart his first year, so it’s certainly possible. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Commanders.com 5 takeaways from Washington’s 20-7 win over the Dolphins 2. Robert Henry Jr. has some juice With Jeremy McNichols out, it created an opportunity for the players down the running back depth chart to show off their skill sets. All the running backs had a solid night, but it was Henry, the undrafted free agent out of UTSA, who stole the show. Henry, who rushed for 2,339 yards in college, showed burst, decisiveness and quickness with the ball in his hands. Although he’s not the biggest player at 196 pounds, he wasn’t afraid to plow up the middle of the defense for dirty yards. He also knows how to separate from defensive players when necessary, and he showed off his 4.5 speed on the Commanders’ opening touchdown. He followed a reach block by sixth-rounder Matt Gulbin and outran the Dolphins’ defense down the sideline for the 22-yard score. Henry ended up leading the Commanders in a 174-yard rushing performance from the group, but an even bigger win for the running back was that he made his case to be on the roster for Week 1. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Sports Illustrated Commanders running back battle just took an interesting turn Kaytron Allen’s 23 carries for 85 yards and a touchdown are another reason Washington’s running back decision remains crowded. Allen handled 45 offensive snaps, more than twice Henry’s workload, including 23 rushing snaps, making his performance more about sustaining a heavy workload than producing the same per-snap efficiency Henry did. Allen finished with a 56.0 overall offensive grade and 61.7 rushing grade, well below Henry’s 72.5 and 73.0 PFF grades. Allen just put an exclamation point on a roster case that was already developing during camp, while Henry is the player who introduced a new name into the four-back equation. Jeremy McNichols did not suit up for the Dolphins game, nor did he participate in the last few days of camp practice . McNichols could lose his spot if his injury lingers, although the trust the team already has in him will likely buy him enough time to compete. McNichols carries weight beyond that trust because the team knows his veteran reliability, familiarity with the offense, and proven ability to handle different responsibilities are hard traits to replace. Friday was just one game against another team’s backups, not the weeks of work of this offseason and training camp. It was also a good gauge of where the personnel is currently. That said, the game changed Henry’s situation completely because he now owns both productive game tape and a favorable independent film grade to go with the practice evaluation Washington already had. The next checkpoint in this battle will be Detroit; if Henry can add another efficient rushing performance and continued special-teams work, it will be much harder to dismiss Miami as a one-night breakout. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE A to Z Sports 6 winners and 3 losers from the Washington Commanders’ preseason win Winner: CB Antonio Hamilton Sr. What can you say about the night Antonio Hamilton Sr. had? It seemed like every time there was a big hit on defense or special teams, Hamilton was leading the way. He finished second on the team with four combined tackles, a tackle for loss, and a pass breakup. This is what Washington knew it was getting when the Commanders re-signed him a few months ago. Hamilton Sr. probably won’t be a starter this year, but he’s a depth guy you can rely upon in tight spots and a good special teams player. Winner: WR Jaylin Lane We know what Lane can do as a returner. The next key development step for him is to prove he can make plays in the passing game, and he did that on Friday night, finishing with a team-leading three catches for 31 yards on four targets with a long of 17. He moved the chains, and that’s an efficient night for a receiver. This bodes well for the Commanders’ receiver room as a whole because, before Stefon Diggs arrived, there were a lot of questions about who was going to be that guy after Terry McLaurin. I’m not saying Lane is going to have a breakout season, but it was very encouraging to see him make those plays in the passing game. Loser: WR Luke McCaffrey Two targets, zero catches, zero yards. McCaffrey looked okay in run blocking, but at this point, his production just has to get better. He hasn’t done anything over his first two seasons in the NFL. He’s got good size, good hands, and the athleticism to play inside and out, but 29 catches for 371 yards and three touchdowns across two seasons is poor. He hasn’t even topped 20 receptions in a single season. Going 0-for-2 in this game is not a good way to start the preseason.  The Bears are entering their fourth week of training camp and have yet to name a starting left tackle.

 Kiran Amegadjie and Jedrick Wills Jr . split reps throughout the Bears' 34-10 win over the Browns in the preseason opener, but it doesn't feel like the team came away with much evidence about which of those two tackles is out in front.

 "Both guys showed some positive traits that you wanted to see from them," offensive coordinator Press Taylor said. "It wasn't perfect. It wasn't as clean as we'd love it to be going forward. And that's kind of why there still continues to be an open competition for the position."

 Coach Ben Johnson achieved his goal of getting similar workloads for both players. Amegadjie logged 34 snaps upon getting the start and came back into the game during the two-minute drill at the end of the first half. That was a challenge for the former third-round pick, who said coming off the bench and being thrown into an unpredictable, fast-paced environment required a higher level of execution.

 Wills got 29 snaps at left tackle, and both players had up-and-down days. As a whole, Chicago's offensive line play was a mixed bag. Tyson Bagent was sacked twice, and quarterbacks Case Keenum and Miller Moss were pressured a total of nine times. The run game wasn't as efficient as Johnson had hoped for and averaged 3.9 yards per carry.

 Johnson stressed the need for Amegadjie and Wills to build consistency. The fact that neither has reached that level isn't lost on the players.

 The Bears activated  Ozzy Trapilo  off the physically unable to perform list on Sunday, seven months after the left tackle ruptured a patellar tendon in the postseason. It is unclear when Trapilo will factor into the mix, but his return with weeks remaining in training camp is a positive sign.

 "It's a little frustrating, but it's also like, it's just that," Amegadjie said. "If I just get that little piece, then I'll be playing at a consistent level the way that I want to be. So it's kind of the life, the ups and downs of playing professional sports, playing football, playing offensive line, and I'm working through that and trying to get better every day."

 In 2025, the Bears waited until cut-down day to announce their starting left tackle. The hope is they'll have tangible evidence soon to determine whom they trust to protect  Caleb Williams ' blind side. That could happen sooner if Braxton Jones returns this week as Johnson forecasted.

 At the time Jones got injured on Aug. 6, he was the front-runner to win the left tackle job. If he's able to reemerge in the competition with the first-team offensive line, and quickly, the Bears might have their answer sooner.

 
 Johnson was short in his response postgame when asked if there was a timeline for  Kyler Gordon 's return to practice. The cornerback has been on the PUP list since July 28 with a calf injury, and the Bears have been reticent about when he's expected back given the delay Gordon has had with his rehab. 
 There's a family reunion on deck for offensive coordinator Press Taylor, whose bother, Zac, is the head coach of the Bengals. The Bears hit the road for a joint practice in Cincinnati on Thursday before next Saturday's preseason game. The trip conjures memories of growing up for Press Taylor. "I remember a lot of times of him dragging me to go outside and play catch, and I didn't want to," the Bears OC said. "And I end up sitting in the front yard, and he's just throwing a ball at me as hard as he could. And that was our idea of playing catch, I guess, for a long time. We played a lot, we had like a 10-yard grass area in the front yard. We played punt return. So, I'm 8, he's 13, and it was him throwing the ball as high as he could, and I would look up and catch it. And we're 10 yards apart, so he just smoked me until I'm trying to catch a punt, basically." 
 

 

 Who is the Bears' top performer so far at camp? 

 What a difference a year makes for Caleb Williams . In his second offseason with Ben Johnson, the quarterback has the Bears' offense in position to be one of the NFL's most explosive units. There are areas he needs to continue to improve in, like with his accuracy, but Williams' command of the playbook has been evident in camp by the chemistry he quickly created with new center Garrett Bradbury and his routine distribution to the likes of tight end Colston Loveland and wide receivers Rome Odunze , Luther Burden III , Zavion Thomas and Kalif Raymond . There hasn't been a single practice over the first half of camp where the offense walked off the field looking like it was in dire straits. Williams' growth and capacity for withstanding a giant install is a big reason why the Bears are in position for their offense to be the catalyst in wins.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Injuries have been a problem in the Bears' secondary. Nickel corner Kyler Gordon is on PUP (calf) with no timeline for his return, safety Coby Bryant is out four-to-six months after knee surgery and the DB depth has been decimated with injuries to Cam Lewis , Terell Smith and Jaylon Jones in addition to top backup safety Elijah Hicks , who remains on PUP. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen will use Chicago's three preseason games to determine his starters are at slot corner and free safety and which backups with little to no NFL experience can be trusted in reserve roles.

 
 Aug. 11 
 Tuesday's practice was about "creating evidence" for the coaching staff to be able to evaluate where players stand in specific roles and who is climbing their way into the 53-man roster.

 "Up to this point, it's been a lot more get the plays in, let's get them repped once or twice and now they can actually execute and go out there and play ball," coach Ben Johnson said. Coaches sent out a game plan Monday night for players to study in hopes of seeing who could play fast and adjust to not knowing what was coming their way.

 With the offense and defense having 98% of their installs in, the 11th practice of camp opened with focusing on short-yardage goal line team drills to build the intensity and competition that Johnson envisioned carrying over to the rest of practice. The starting offense dominated that period with chunk runs from  D'Andre Swift  and Kyle Monangai , who each scored. In the first move-the-ball period, Swift got loose and found his way down the right sideline for a 62-yard TD.

 Quarterback Caleb Williams  and the starters aced a tough test towards the end of practice with the offense backed up at its own 1-yard line. The goal for the drill was to get two first downs, which Williams accomplished by creating space to find Rome Odunze for a 50-plus yard catch-and-run followed by a big gain to Scotty Miller .

 Both the first and second-team offenses weren't as crisp in the situational drills at the end of practice, but Williams exited practice feeling confident in his ability to adjust on the fly and stack…

title: 2026 Green Bay Packers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Packers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Packers reporter Rob Demovsky has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Packers camp. Will the revamped WR corps help QB Jordan Love and the offense take another step? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Packers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news out of Packers camp 
 
 CB Keisean Nixon not guaranteed starting role with Packers 
 Aaron Rodgers wishes game at Lambeau, discusses retirement return 
 Packers QB Love expected to play in first preseason game 
 Micah Parsons: Playing vs. Cowboys in Week 6 'realistic' 
 Packers RT changes last name to Bako-Bewele to honor heritage 
 Packers star TE Tucker Kraft activated off PUP after ACL recovery 
 Packers CEO: Team needs financial bump to stay competitive 
 

 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 16 

 How eager was Tucker Kraft to get on the practice field Sunday? He was the first player out of the Don Hutson Center and onto the practice field. The reason? He was finally cleared to do 11-on-11 team drills. While Kraft had returned to practice on July 31, he had been limited only to individual drills as he continued his comeback from last year's ACL surgery.

 Kraft caught all five of the passes thrown his way in practice, including one touchdown that prompted an emphatic spike and his chest-bumping, starfish celebration.

 The fourth-year tight end who tore his ACL in Week 9 last season has made no secret of his desire for a contract extension. He's in the final year of his rookie contract. He said he never considered skipping any 11-on-11s until he got his deal.

 "Well, that's a whole part of this process, is me day in and day out, coming in and being consistent, stacking days without setbacks and accumulating these reps now in a team setting so that they can see my health and we can just keep taking the talks from there," Kraft said.

 However, he said he hopes to have a contract extension done before the Sept. 13 opener against the Vikings.

 "That's the goal," Kraft said. "I think we're a different team when I'm out on the field and I think that's obvious. I think everyone in this organization, every fan knows that, without sounding arrogant.

 "I've kinda gone through life, just taking things blow by blow, assuming things will always just work out in the end. So me, the preparation, the sacrifices I've made to be here right now, I'm just going to continue to assume that it's all going to work out for me."

 

 
 On more than one occasion, defensive players got too close to quarterback Jordan Love . Late in practice, coach Matt LaFleur had finally seen it one too many times. He tossed Barryn Sorrell from a team period after Sorrell bull-rushed tackle Anthony Belton right into Love. 
 Belton took some snaps at left tackle with the starters late in practice. So did John Williams after starter Jordan Morgan appeared to be limited. 
 The defense came up with three interceptions: Brandon Cisse undercut an out route by Matthew Golden that Love slightly underthrew, Kitan Oladapo picked off Love to end a two-minute period and Jaylin Simpson picked off Tyrod Taylor with an over-the-shoulder interception deep down the sideline. 
 It took 12 practices, but the Packers finally had their first scuffles of training camp. First, it was running back Chris Brooks and linebacker Zaire Franklin . Later, defensive tackle Chris McClellan pushed running back Damien Martinez into another play, prompting offensive lineman Dalton Cooper and defensive lineman Nazir Stackhouse to get into it. 
 Trey Smack backed up his perfect performance in the preseason opener by making all four field goal attempts on Sunday. Including his 3-for-3 game against the Steelers, the rookie kicker is 27-for-35 on all competitive field goals. 
 Lukas Van Ness (shoulder) and Darian Kinnard (ankle) were new to the DNP list. Van Ness, who played three snaps against the Steelers, said he actually banged his shoulder in practice last week. 
 The Packers hosted the Menasha High School football team at Sunday's practice. The Bluejays stadium was partially destroyed by the July 27 tornado that hit the area and will play their home games at Lawrence University in Appleton. LaFleur brought the Bluejays players into the post-practice huddle and several Packers players posed for pictures with the Menasha players. 
 

 

 Friday, Aug. 14 

 Friday's media sessions with the defensive coaches left one thing clear: Keisean Nixon is not guaranteed a starting job.

 
It's an unusual position for a player coming off a Pro Bowl appearance, but based on what was said -- and what wasn't said -- Nixon has not done enough to lock up the starting outside cornerback job he held all of last season.

 
This after Nixon (along with safety Kitan Oladapo ) whiffed on a tackle that turned a short gain into a 25-yard catch-and-run by Germie Bernard and gave up another completion during a 19-play stint in Thursday's preseason opener against the Steelers. Officially, Nixon was credited with one tackle.

 
"We have a corner competition," secondary coach Bobby Babich said when asked what's going on with Nixon.

 
Babich added that every position has competition, but compared with how the coaches talked about Nixon, the praise for rookie Brandon Cisse and veteran free agent addition  Benjamin St-Juste was effusive.

 
Said Babich of second-rounder Cisse, who started at the other cornerback spot opposite Nixon on Thursday: "Habit-wise he's ahead of the game as far as when it comes to rookies. Guy's a film junkie. Wants to be really good."

 
Cisse played 19 snaps, the same number as Nixon, and had three tackles (including one on special teams).

 
St-Juste played 24 snaps with the backups and recorded two tackles.

 
"He showed yesterday that he will really put his body on some guys," cornerbacks coach Daniel Bullocks said of St-Juste. "Been really impressed."

 
The best anyone offered about Nixon was how he has handled the competition.

 
"He's handled it great," Babich said. "He's locked in. Every player is going to have plays they want back."

 Other observations: 

 
 Speaking of competitions, there appears to be a new one brewing on the offensive line. It had been assumed by most that when Aaron Banks (knee) returned to 11-on-11 drills, the left guard job would be his, like it was last year. But while the veteran has been given rest days and limited to individual drills, rookie Jager Burton has played better and better. "I think he's going to make it extremely difficult," coach Matt LaFleur said of the decision at left guard. "I think Jager has done a really good job. I think not only him but [Jacob] Monk ." 
 Lukas Van Ness played only three snaps but had what defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon called two "wins" -- one against the run and one for a sack. "Lukas has been having an excellent camp," Gannon said. "He's a very versatile player, and he can win in a lot of different areas." How well Van Ness and the other edge rushers play until Micah Parsons comes back from his torn left ACL might determine how the Packers fare early in the season. Fellow edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr . also had a sack early in the game. 
 LaFleur said running back Josh Jacobs (groin) could "potentially" return to practice this coming week but added "it wouldn't be until later in the week." 
 The Packers don't practice Saturday but resume open training camp practices Sunday. 
 

 

 Who is the Packers' top performer so far at camp? 

 Not that Xavier McKinney didn't play well last…

title: Five Patriots who stood out in their first preseason game
summary: From Kyle Williams to K.J. Britt, here are the players whose performances should have them ascending the Patriots' ranks.
full_text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- Quick-hit thoughts and notes around the New England Patriots and the NFL:

 1. High five: The Patriots didn't play the majority of their starters in the preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts (a  13-13 tie ), so there weren't many seismic revelations about the team. It was mostly a game about developing depth and getting a first look at rookies.

 With this in mind, here are five players whose performances appear to have them ascending -- or at least worthy of closer evaluation in their quest to earn a role on the team:

 LB K.J. Britt 
 When the six-year veteran was signed to a one-year, $1.4 million contract in March, the projection was that he was likely to fill the void created by Jack Gibbens ' free agent departure to Arizona. That role is as a top backup and core special teamer, but Britt seemed to be overtaken by Chad Muma and undrafted rookie Khalil Jacobs before what could represent a turnaround for Britt on Thursday.

 The 6-foot, 240-pound Britt started, had a tackle behind the line of scrimmage that showcased his ability to play downhill with force, and then followed it up on the next play by chasing down quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr . and forcing a fumble, which Patriots teammate Isaiah Iton recovered. Britt played 14 defensive snaps and five on special teams.

 "K.J. showed up with a veteran presence, physical presence, trying to help us on special teams and add versatility [by] trying to play both positions inside," coach Mike Vrabel said, referencing middle and weakside linebacker. "I have appreciated how he approached the offseason and now he's been given a chance to compete."

 

 RB Jam Miller 
 The seventh-round pick from Alabama seemed more likely to wind up on the practice squad when training camp began, but his chances of making the roster improved after the Patriots placed leading RB3 candidate Terrell Jennings on injured reserve before Thursday's game.

 The 5-foot-10, 209-pound Miller started and played 22 snaps, totaling 55 yards on 14 carries (3.9 yards per carry) with some hard-charging running that included converting one short-yardage fourth-down rushing attempt behind first-round rookie right tackle  Caleb Lomu .

 "I felt like he ran with his pads down and had a couple physical runs, and was happy for him," coach Mike Vrabel said. "This is a great evaluation. We can start to figure out guys that can and start to figure out guys that can't, too."

 Miller providing more special teams impact could help solidify his standing. Newly signed running back Hassan Haskins steamrolled his assignment on his initial snap on kickoff coverage -- the type of play that typically catches the attention of coaches.

 QB Behren Morton 
 One lingering question is whether the Patriots will keep three quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, or just two, with the third layer of depth coming from the practice squad.

 Morton totaled 30 snaps, all in the second half. The playcalling was mostly conservative (a lot of slants) as he finished 7-of-13 for 66 yards. Morton wasn't overwhelmed on the final drive -- ball on the 27-yard line with 1:10 left -- in helping get the Patriots in position for a 49-yard field goal attempt that could have won the game with two completions (while aided by a questionable unnecessary roughness penalty). It was a reflection that the moment wasn't too big for him.

 "Trying to prove a point to be on this team," Morton said. "I think if you show you know what you are doing, that [earns] respect from the veterans."

 

 Edge  Bradyn Swinson 
 The 6-foot-4, 255-pound Swinson played behind starters Gabe Jacas and 2026 seventh-round pick Quintayvious Hutchins , so his most extensive work didn't come until the second half. His power rush contributed to pressuring quarterback Riley Leonard on a pass intercepted by John Saunders Jr ., and Swinson later had a batted pass on fourth down, which essentially caused another turnover.

 Swinson played 38 snaps, the third-highest total among defenders, with three tackles and one quarterback hit. He is in the mix for a roster spot behind starters Dre'Mont Jones , Harold Landry III (currently on PUP), Elijah Ponder and Jacas.

 WR Kyle Williams 
 The 2025 third-round pick showcased his route-running acumen with what television announcers (and former Patriots) Devin and Jason McCourty referred to as a "killer crossover" move on his 12-yard touchdown catch from quarterback Tommy DeVito . Williams later had a crisp comeback route for a 25-yard gain.

 It wasn't all perfect. Williams was penalized for offensive pass interference by blocking too early on a quick pass, and he didn't come back for another deep pass that could have drawn a defensive pass interference penalty. That led to immediate on-field coaching from Vrabel.

 But overall, Williams' potential was on display, which included him playing gunner on the punt coverage team -- an opportunity to showcase his speed in what could be a tiebreaker for a spot on the game-day roster in a crowded receiver room.

 Asked what areas Williams can focus on after Thursday's game, Vrabel noted his confidence and being more of a presence inside the numbers and on intermediate routes.

 

 2. Response needed: In contrast to the five aforementioned players, here are three who will likely be looking to shake off some rust:

 
 S Mike Brown : He was initially projected as a top backup behind  Kevin Byard  and Craig Woodson , but now  Dell Pettus  could have the inside track for the role. He was shaken at the top of one route for an 18-yard gain to set up the Colts' first touchdown. 
 OL James Hudson III : He is a career tackle who might be out of his comfort level at guard, but the Patriots are thin on depth there and would ideally be able to turn to him if needed. Hudson gave up multiple pressures, including one that led to a sack of DeVito. 
 LB  Chad Muma : He has been the top backup behind starters Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss , but among his hiccups was overrunning a play in the flat late in the second quarter. 
 
 3. Gonzalez contract: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez posted a congratulatory Instagram message to Seahawks cornerback Devon Witherspoon on Saturday for agreeing to a four-year, $132 million contract extension . The deal provides a framework for Gonzalez's possible extension in New England. ESPN's Adam Schefter tweeted  that the sides "have not made much progress so far". 

 Gonzalez, meanwhile, has remained out of practice since Tuesday after appearing to injure his ankle while defending receiver Romeo Doubs on a touchdown pass.

 4. Doubs coming on: With three tightly contested touchdown receptions in Saturday's practice -- the final one he tossed high in the air in celebration -- Doubs continued to build momentum. He had some of his best practices last week.

 "I think just new offense, new year, figuring out the player, getting to know him. Really, a lot of positive things, trending in the right direction," Vrabel said of Doubs while also noting the work of receivers coach Todd Downing.

 "Todd is very conscientious about each one of his players, what each of them needs to learn the offense, where they need to be, what routes are going to be really good for them and the decisions that they need to make. I think he found where Rome can really help us -- be big, fast and aggressive."

 

 5. Eagles week: This might be the Patriots' most important week of the preseason, highlighted by two practices with the Eagles on Wednesday and Thursday, then a home game against them Saturday. After a full-pads session that featured a lot of red zone work Saturday, the team is scheduled to have lower-tempo workouts Sunday and Tuesday, sandwiched around a higher-intensity practice Monday.

 "It's a grind; we're deep into camp now. We're in it," running back Rhamondre Stevenson said of the stretch of six straight days of work.

 6. Crowd buzz: Preseason games often don't create much buzz late in the fourth…
