title: 2026 Pittsburgh Steelers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Steelers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Steelers camp. How will coach Mike McCarthy shape this roster and the offense in his first year in Pittsburgh? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Steelers' top camp performer and biggest lingering questions.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Steelers camp 
 
 Steelers' Benton agrees to 4-year, $72M extension 
 Rookies Drew Allar, Will Howard 'very poised' in Steelers' preseason win 
 Steelers bring back veteran LB Roberts on one-year deal 
 'Tempered': Inside Mike McCarthy's new vision for Steelers 
 Steelers' Broderick Jones cleared after eight months (neck) 
 Rodgers: 'Zero debate' 2026 will be last season 
 
 

 Sunday, Aug. 16 
 The Steelers' eighth and final install wrapped up with a bang Sunday afternoon.

 In the final team period, rookie safety Robert Spears-Jennings lowered his shoulder into wide receiver Max Hurleman as Hurleman made a play to cross the goal line. The hit sent Hurleman flying, and as the wide receiver slowly got up, tight end Lance Mason  got in Spears-Jennings' face. Once on his feet, Hurleman joined Mason and shoved Spears-Jennings.

 Seconds later, several others ran over and a fight broke out, with pockets of several skirmishes. The seeds for the altercation, though, were planted several plays before the hit. Guard Mason McCormick chirped at recently signed inside linebacker Elandon Roberts for having "fresh legs" when he felt Roberts crossed a line with a hard hit of wide receiver Levi Wentz .

 "Everybody just been going for so long," safety Jaquan Brisker said afterward, acknowledging that a scrum like that was typical at the end of training camp. "You know how everybody just been in camp, body, things like that. Stuff happens there. ... It's physical. I mean, that's part of the game. You can't take that away from the game. Even it happens on game day, sometimes.

 "... You want some dogs out there. You rather have a dog than tell somebody to keep going or whatever, then bite. But guys are out there ready to play, ready to go. Got some dogs out there for sure."

 More observations: 

 
 Rookie seventh-round pick Eli Heidenreich won the team's annual home run derby Saturday night. The Mt. Lebanon, Pennsylvania, native played baseball in high school, but he admitted that he hadn't swung a bat in at least four or five years. "Don't know if I ever poked one out in a game," he said. "I was more of like a contact hitter." 
 Special teams coordinator Danny Crossman said some of the penalties called against his units in Thursday's preseason game were technique issues that can be easily corrected. Others, though, he characterized as "things that take no talent," and he wants to eliminate those from the game. "We can't give away field position with penalties," he said Sunday. "We can't waste opportunities with substitution errors. So, things that you don't ever want to see that sometimes pop up in the first preseason game, but that stuff has to be eliminated from our game." 
 Despite the threat of stormy weather Sunday, the Steelers held their final installation practice outside and went through the two-hour practice as scheduled. "The only thing that's going to take me off the field is lightning," coach Mike McCarthy said. "If it's 8 miles, 8½, that's close enough. So, it's just being practical about it. That's my line between toughness and stupidity." 
 Rookie WR and kick returner Kaden Wetjen returned to practice Sunday after being sidelined Saturday. The rest of the banged-up players, including WRs Michael Pittman Jr . and DK Metcalf , didn't practice. 
 Safety DeShon Elliott had his longest day of participation as he works back from last season's knee injury. He was also involved in the end-of-practice scrum, shoving tight end Jaheim Bell . "The physicality showed up today, I know that," defensive coordinator Patrick Graham said. "And then just he's always active in the meetings. He's active bringing the guys together. He's a solid communicator, and that's what we need with that position." 
 

 

 Who has been the Steelers' top performer so far at camp? 
 DB  Asante Samuel Jr . He immensely benefitted from Joey Porter Jr .'s stint on the PUP list with back soreness in the midst of extension negotiations. With his increased playing time, Samuel made play after play in Latrobe, including several PBUs in two-minute drills and against wide receiver DK Metcalf .

 Samuel, whom coach Mike McCarthy said was one of his "favorite" players since arriving in Pittsburgh, was a late add last season coming off of neck surgery, and he signed a one-year, $4 million deal to stay with the Steelers in free agency. If his camp performance is any indication, Samuel's value will be significantly higher than his cost.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How does this new-look defense operate under defensive coordinator Patrick Graham? While there's plenty of questions about how Aaron Rodgers and the offense will look with McCarthy, perhaps more important to the team's success this season is Graham's ability to bring a fresh perspective and scheme to the NFL's highest-paid defense. Of course Graham won't show all of his tricks in the preseason, but these games will give an early preview of the defensive communication and the quality of depth across the board.

 

 Saturday, Aug. 15 

 Keeanu Benton knew good news must be coming when his agent told him to give him a call at 10 p.m. on Friday. And that's just what the Steelers' defensive lineman got as his agent informed him that the team was giving the 2023 second-round pick a four-year, $72 million extension .

 "I was in my bed actually," Benton said Saturday afternoon after officially signing his contract. "Then my agent told me to call him and I assumed, because you're not about to tell me to call you for no reason when I'm about to go to bed."

 Benton's agent also added outside linebacker Nick Herbig to the call to share the good news. Not only do the two share the same agent, but they've been best friends since playing together at Wisconsin.

 "Me and Nick stayed up for a little bit just talking and reflecting on how far we came," Benton said, adding that he didn't sleep much after getting the news. "That seven years done went by kind of fast, but we made a lot of progress within it."

 Earlier this offseason, Benton stood in the back of the room during a news conference following Herbig's $100 million extension . Saturday, Herbig, whom the Steelers drafted in the fourth round the same year, returned the favor.

 "We've been best friends since the day we met in college," Herbig said. "That's my brother. Everything we've been through together -- and seeing him, all the trials and hardships, grinding, going through the mud together, and getting drafted together -- this journey we've been on. I can't even put it into words, man, how it feels."

 More observations: 

 
 The Steelers had a light walkthrough on Saturday with practice lasting less than an hour. 
 DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr . didn't participate after sustaining undisclosed injuries earlier in training camp. McCarthy said the two would be "hard pressed" to work this week, suggesting that it's unlikely either will play against the New York Jets on Friday. If that's the case, it's also unlikely Aaron Rodgers will play because McCarthy has stressed the importance of playing certain combinations together, including WR1-WR2-QB1. 
 Chief of staff…

title: 2026 Seattle Seahawks training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Seahawks training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. The  Seattle Seahawks ' camp is taking place in Renton, Washington, and Seahawks reporter Brady Henderson has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Seahawks camp. What is new with the defending Super Bowl champions? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Packers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Seahawks camp 
 
 WR Tory Horton healthy after cracking tibia last season 
 Seattle Pro Bowl DL Williams confirms deal talks 
 Seattle's Nick Emmanwori has ankle surgery, expected to play W1 
 Who are the Khoslas? Meet the family set to buy the Seahawks 
 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 16 
 One lesser-known player who's making his best case for a job with the Seahawks in 2026 is Montorie Foster Jr . The second-year receiver continued his strong summer with a touchdown catch in Seattle's preseason opener, a 17-7 loss to the Dallas Cowboys .

 This time last year, he was unsigned and thinking about giving up football.

 Foster joined the Seahawks as an undrafted free agent in 2025. But after he hurt his hamstring and was waived with an injury designation in early August, he returned home to Cleveland and began looking for regular jobs. He got his real estate license and even worked as a substitute teacher at St. Edward High School, his alma mater.

 "I had a Latin class," he said postgame. "I don't know any Latin, at all."

 But Foster appears to know what it "carpe diem" means, because he's grabbing a hold of his latest opportunity with Seattle. The Seahawks brought him back to their practice squad in December, signed him to a futures deal after the Super Bowl and are now seeing him make a serious push to stick around in some capacity.

 "Every time I play, I play to a standard and it don't matter if I'm playing good or bad, my standard is my standard," he said. "I go out there every day and just try to put my best foot forward every day and put forth the effort, go block, do the little things and let everything else take care of itself."

 Foster makes at least one play virtually every day. On Saturday, he almost made two. After catching a 5-yard touchdown from Drew Lock to cap Seattle's opening drive, he got open on a go route down the sideline for what would have been another score had Lock not overthrown him.

 "The journey he's been on from the previous year until now, man, he's light-years away from where he was, and he's been fantastic for us," Lock said. "He makes great plays. Explosive with the ball in his hand. Reliable. He's going to catch the ball. Yeah, nothing but confidence for him."

 It'll be tough for Foster to make Seattle's 53-man roster. Tory Horton is healthy and one of the league's more overqualified No. 4 receivers behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba , Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed . The Seahawks gave Jake Bobo a two-year, $5.5 million deal, so he's making the team. Even if they keep a sixth receiver, Cody White would also be in play for that spot.

 But based on the frequency with which he's made plays, Foster looks like someone the Seahawks would at least like to keep on their practice squad, if they can get him there. Whether it's in Seattle or elsewhere, he should be on an NFL team this fall and not at the front of a Latin class.

 "It means everything," Foster said of his opportunity. "I was back at home for 16 weeks and it was tough. There were times where I wanted to give up and get a regular job. But I stayed at it. My dad told me that cream always rises to the top and to just stay faithful. I just kept working, and now I'm here today."

 More observations: 

 
 Mike Macdonald was less than pleased with how the Seahawks played against Dallas, saying their operation and the way they finished plays was not up to their standard. "That's the most people I've ever seen at a preseason game," he said of the fans at Lumen Field. "We owe them a better performance, to say the least." 
 With Sam Darnold and virtually every other Seahawks starter not playing, Drew Lock and Jalen Milroe rotated. Lock went 9-of-13 for 40 yards and the TD to Foster. Milroe went 5-of-8 for 36 yards and added 36 rushing yards on five carries. Macdonald's assessment of the QBs: "Good enough to put up seven points. Got to put up more points. We need to operate better. There's some good things. It's great to have tape against another team now. In a different type of setting where the pass rush is live, you're up against the play clock. All these different things that you have to be able to play out are great learning experiences for everybody, quarterbacks included." 
 Macdonald had praise for backup LB Tyrice Knight , who led all players with 10 tackles and had two passes defensed: "We're a little banged up at inside 'backer, so T-Knight probably played more than we bargained for. But he was the best player on the field on defense today, for sure, so that was cool to see." 
 Macdonald has called defensive plays in each of his first two seasons and will do so again in 2026, but he let DC Aden Durde handle those duties Saturday, as he has done in past preseason games. "It's a great experience for AD," Macdonald said. "He's called the majority of camp up to this point. He's done a phenomenal job throughout camp. He really has. We've had a ton of call-it periods. He's on the details, just doing a lot of great stuff, honestly. But at some point, I've got to get ready to call a game too, so I think I'll probably call next week." 
 

 

 Who has been the Seahawks' top performer so far at camp? 
 The offense in general has been impressive considering the transition to new coordinator Brian Fleury and the fact that it faces the league's best scoring defense from 2025 every day in practice. In terms of individuals, we'll give the nod to Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The league's leading receiver from last season and the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year has remained an almost-unstoppable force. Rashid Shaheed is the deep threat in Seattle's offense, but QB  Sam Darnold has connected with JSN on several downfield shots this summer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will win the third cornerback job? After letting Riq Woolen leave in free agency, the Seahawks have Noah Igbinoghene and Nehemiah Pritchett competing to replace him. Macdonald demands physicality from his corners, so preseason games (and Seattle's joint practice this week against the Titans) could be the differentiator in this battle. Regardless of who emerges, the position looks like a question mark, which is why Seattle is looking into free agent corner Terrion Arnold , who was released by the Lions in June after being arrested on felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping.

 
 

 Friday, Aug. 14 
 After 15 practices and three walk-throughs over the first three weeks of training camp, the Seahawks are set to open the preseason Saturday night against the Dallas Cowboys at Lumen Field.

 "Our players have earned the right ... to go let it rip and trust your training and go have fun," coach Mike Macdonald said Friday. "Go play football [like] they know how and our brand of ball, and hopefully it comes to life, and hopefully we have some cost-of-doing-business celebration penalties."

 Macdonald said many of the team's established starters will not play. That includes Sam Darnold , whose only preseason action last summer was 10 snaps in the second game. Drew Lock will start against Dallas and Jalen Milroe will play next, and in a change from a year…

title: 2026 San Francisco 49ers training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from 49ers training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. 49ers reporter Nick Wagoner has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at 49ers camp. What does  Mike Evans  look like as a top receiver on the 49ers? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the 49ers' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp previews for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from 49ers' camp 
 
 Can the 49ers depend on rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling? 
 49ers' Ricky Pearsall has knee surgery, targets 9-month recovery 
 How the 49ers' defense looks different under Raheem Morris 
 Kyle Shanahan nears full strength, plans to coach preseason opener 
 Kittle eyes opener in Australia 
 
 

 

 Sunday, Aug. 16 

 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa hasn't practiced since Aug. 3. In fact, Bosa hadn't been spotted on the practice field doing work on the side since then. Until Sunday.

 Though Bosa, who has been battling soreness and tendinitis as he recovers from a torn ACL, did not return to practice, he went through an extensive workout on a side field. Niners coach Kyle Shanahan said Tuesday that Bosa is dealing with "a pretty normal thing with ACLs," but given Bosa's injury history and that he was practicing before the soreness, it seemed to be a setback.

 "We have to be smart here from week to week," Shanahan said. "But no concerns about him."

 Though there are still hurdles to clear before Bosa returns to practice, Sunday was, at minimum, a notable step forward.

 
 Three 49ers were added to the nonparticipant list Sunday: G Dominick Puni is in concussion protocol, defensive tackle Gracen Halton has an ankle injury and WR Demarcus Robinson missed the session for undisclosed reasons. 
 DT C.J. West and DE Titus Leo were hurt on back-to-back plays during a team drill. Both limped to the locker room and did not return. 
 WR  Deebo Samuel Sr . and WR Jacob Cowing were also shaken up at various points but returned and finished the session. 
 QB Kurtis Rourke did not practice again after he left last week's preseason opener because of breathing trouble. It's unclear what his injury is, but OC Klay Kubiak indicated that Rourke won't be out long. 
 With Puni out, Robert Jones worked at right guard as Jones, Connor Colby and Carver Willis continue to push for the starting left guard job. 
 Undrafted rookie DT James Thompson Jr . has been an under-the-radar surprise in camp and got some extra looks with the starters after West went down. 
 CB Renardo Green took issue with an official after he was whistled for a couple of penalties in red zone work. He got a flag for defensive pass interference then one for defensive holding. When he successfully defended a third pass thrown his way, he asked the official why he didn't throw a third flag. 
 Cowing had, perhaps, the best play of the day, laying out for a deep ball down the middle from QB Brock Purdy for the catch and a big gain. 
 

 

 Who is the 49ers' top performer so far at camp? 
 QB Brock Purdy . There are others deserving of mention here, but this has been Purdy's best and most consistent training camp despite working with a constantly changing supporting cast. No matter who has been at running back or receiver, Purdy has found ways to move the offense in nearly every practice. He has been particularly sharp when pushing the ball downfield for big plays. If healthy, he looks poised for a big year.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where's the pass rush coming from? The Niners were last in the NFL in sacks (20) and 31st in pressures (157) in 2025. In the offseason, they traded for defensive tackle Osa Odighizuwa ; they used draft picks on edge Romello Height and defensive tackle Gracen Halton . All three should help, but with defensive ends Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams not yet back from ACL surgeries, the exhibition slate will be the time for others to step forward and carve out roles.

 
 Saturday, Aug. 15 
 For the 49ers offense, there aren't many obviously available spots in the starting lineup. The exception comes at left guard where the competition is growing larger rather than narrowing as the season approaches.

 In Saturday's practice, the Niners added rookie Carver Willis to the mix after Connor Colby and Robert Jones have spent the first few weeks of camp rotating with the starting unit. Colby went first but in the next set of snaps, it was Willis working next to left tackle Trent Williams . Nobody has separated there so far and it was tough sledding blocking DT Osa Odighizuwa in this session, which means any formal decision is going to take some time.

 "Those guys are competing," Williams said. "It's a three-man race, so may the best man win, but they're all playing their butts off. Carver is the youngest and he got a little more to learn, but he has a high ceiling, a lot of potential. So just can't wait to see how he develops."

 More observations: 

 
 WR Jacob Cowing returned from his hip flexor injury and made a deep catch down the sideline in team drills. 
 CB Jack Jones was back at practice after injuring his hand early in Thursday's preseason opener. Jones recovered a fumble early in practice. 
 Still no RB Christian McCaffrey or DE Nick Bosa as they recover from some soreness and tendinitis, respectively. 
 Injured RBs Kaelon Black (adductor) and Jordan James (ribs) did some work on the side during the practice, the first time James has been seen since the injury early in camp. 
 QB Kurtis Rourke , who went to the hospital at halftime of Thursday's game because of a hit to the ribs and subsequent breathing problems, did not practice but was on the sideline watching and seemingly in good spirits. 
 With Dre Greenlaw only doing individual drills Saturday, rookie Jaden Dugger continued to get work with the starters at weak side linebacker. Dugger has made a strong impression on defensive coordinator Raheem Morris in the first few weeks and seems to have a good shot at a role in the defense early on. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 More than two weeks into camp, the 49ers offense was looking forward to seeing how it would fare against another team Tuesday. The answer? Quite well.

 After a slow start for the unit, QB Brock Purdy continued his strong camp by carving through the Titans secondary for much of the joint practice session, particularly in the latter half of the session. I had Purdy at 21-of-27 on the day, including multiple touchdown passes and no interceptions.

 

 His best throws came in a move in which he dropped a perfect ball between three defenders to rookie WR De'Zhaun Stribling that would have gone for a long touchdown. And then, he had another layered throw over linebacker Cody Barton for a big gain to TE Jake Tonges .

 Even Purdy's toughest critic had to give it up for him after the practice.

 "Brock's a really good player, so I expect him to have good plays," coach Kyle Shanahan said. "I notice all the bad plays ... I didn't notice many bad plays today so I think he had a hell of a day."

 More observations: 

 
 There were a handful of fights early in the practice that looked like they might have ended the day early. San Francisco's defense seemed to be doing most of the early agitating. But both sides settled in and got some good work. 
 Stribling showed that his early flashes aren't limited to producing against his teammates. Regardless of which unit he was working against, he repeatedly made big plays. 
 Veteran WR Demarcus Robinson also had another big day, catching a couple of touchdowns from Purdy and continuing to make the case to be a valuable backup…

title: Why Titans believe Daboll can maximize Ward's potential
summary: The Titans are looking for the Cam Ward-Brian Daboll relationship to be as effective as what Daboll enjoyed in Buffalo.
full_text:
NASHVILLE, Tenn. -- As someone who's been tasked with developing plans to ruin days for opposing quarterbacks, Tennessee Titans head coach Robert Saleh -- a former defensive coordinator -- is well aware of when they're most effective.

 He saw firsthand in his previous stop as a head coach with the New York Jets how much the team relies on a quarterback playing well. Saleh's time featured a defense that finished in the top five in fewest yards allowed in 2022 and 2023. While the defense was elite, the Jets failed to make the playoffs mostly because of an inefficient offense, starting with the quarterback.

 It's no coincidence that one of Saleh's first moves after becoming the Titans coach Jan. 20 was hiring offensive coordinator Brian Daboll seven days later to maximize the talent Cam Ward flashed down the stretch last season after being the No. 1 pick in 2025. Saleh's success with the Titans will depend in large part on how well Ward performs in three specific areas outlined by Saleh at the start of training camp.

 "The quarterback metric is third down, red zone, two-minute [drill]," Saleh said. "Those are the three categories where the quarterback shines and pulls the team along.

 "When it comes to third down, everyone knows you're about to throw. In two-minute, you got to have it. In the red zone, everything's sped up, and the windows get a lot tighter. That's where the quarterback shines."

 Daboll's previous experience should give the Titans hope of improving in third-down conversions and red zone touchdown scoring percentage.

 The Buffalo Bills had the league's 30th-ranked third-down conversion rate (31.63%) in  Josh Allen 's rookie season with Daboll as the offensive coordinator in 2018. Daboll and quarterbacks coach Shea Tierney helped Allen and the offense rise to the fourth-best rate two years later in 2020 (46.64%) and finish second only to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs in 2021 (47.33%).

 

 Daboll goes over a multitude of scenarios to help Ward make an informed decision in clutch situations. That's why Daboll consults with Bennie Contrino, whom the Titans hired in July to be the team's director of strategy and analytics.

 They looked at various scenarios over the last five years, such as down-and-distance, time left on the clock, where the ball is placed and more. It was all broken down into percentages and presented to the quarterbacks because things change drastically in third-down situations.

 "How you perform on early downs can really help you in those situations," Daboll said. "Once you get to third-and-4-plus [yards], it's significantly an advantage for a defense. And that's any defense. So you try to stay out of those situations, but when you're in them, everything's not going to be perfect.

 "There's a lot of bullets flying. Different pressures, disguises, looks. And it's not always going to be perfect on third down."

 Defensive coordinator Gus Bradley added that third down comes down to creativity.

 "It all comes back to affecting the quarterback and getting him off schedule and getting those third-and-7, 8, 9, 10 ranges rather than living in third-and-2 to 3 or third-and-3 to 4," Bradley said. "You'll see different nuances, different things that maybe you wouldn't see on first and second down."

 Daboll will be tasked with helping Ward and the Titans make a similar jump in third-down percentage after the offense posted a 31.9% conversion rate last season, ranking Tennessee second-worst in the NFL. Ward shared on the "Deebo and Joe" podcast that the main thing he has learned under Daboll was how success as a quarterback is heavily influenced by their performance on third down.

 "Those are downs that can win or lose you the game," Ward said during training camp. "It's when quarterbacks are paid the most to be successful on. It's where it has to click for you if it doesn't click on first or second down.

 "You gotta have an awareness of situational football because that's when it matters the most."

 

 Third-down improvement was one of the key reasons free agent receiver Wan'Dale Robinson was a priority for the Titans in March. Robinson excelled from the slot position for Daboll over the past two seasons with the New York Giants .

 "That's where I like to think I make a lot of my money is on third down," Robinson told ESPN. "Just being able to always be open and catch anything and everything."

 Daboll's offense in Buffalo also saw great improvement in red zone touchdown scoring percentage. The Bills jumped from 16th in the league (59.46%) in 2018 to No. 1 in 2021 by scoring touchdowns on 66.28% of their visits inside the 20-yard line.

 Tennessee could use a similar boost in red zone scoring after finishing 13th last season. Sure, 13th isn't bad, but the Titans ranked 30th with 16.7 points per game. That average would look better if they had managed to get into the end zone more than 57.58% of the time last year.

 Allen credited Daboll for the Bills' red zone efficiency improvement by simplifying reads, tailoring quarterback run packages and trusting Allen's physical decision-making in the condensed space inside the 20-yard line.

 Current Titans backup quarterback Mitchell Trubisky was the backup for the Bills when their offense peaked in third-down conversions and red zone scoring percentage. Trubisky feels Daboll does a great job of helping the quarterback find the balance of making plays but also limiting turnovers.

 He mentioned how Daboll emphasizes not trying to force throws and, at times, just taking what the defense gives you to get to the next play.

 "You don't take away a kid's natural ability, his talent to make plays on the run, but you got to eliminate the turnovers," Trubisky told ESPN. "Let's not force [a play] and put our defense in a bad spot [after a turnover]. Let's maybe throw underneath and make the defense tackle."

 Ward already likes the way Daboll has shown trust in him to use his playmaking ability in clutch situations.

 "I think this system is a young guy's system that gives us a lot of freelance," Ward said. "It gives myself and the receivers freedom to do as we feel space-wise.

 "He warns me when I need to be a better decision-maker, but he never holds me back. He always wants me to go out there and be a confident gunslinger, whether that's throwing it down the field, checking it down or throwing it across the middle. It's been great. Coach Dabes lets me be me."

title: Mets troll Jayden Daniels over LSU NIL dispute
summary: The team is the latest to poke fun at Daniels over his jersey number dispute with his alma mater, LSU.
full_text:
Jayden Daniels is getting trolled ... by the New York Mets , of all teams.

 The Washington Commanders quarterback has been embroiled in an unusual dispute with his alma mater, LSU . Daniels' spokesperson told ESPN that the quarterback took issue with the Tigers allowing cornerback DJ Pickett to wear the No. 5 jersey that Daniels donned during his Heisman-winning season in 2023. Daniels' attorney has informed LSU that it can no longer use his name, image and likeness, according to an Aug. 5 letter sent to Tigers athletic director Verge Ausberry, a copy of which was obtained by ESPN on Wednesday.

 The dispute has become fodder for internet trolling. StubHub announced it would "no longer offer tickets in groups of 5." NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series team TRICON Garage said it would not be running No. 5 at a race Friday. The account for Minor League Baseball made a joke about a postponed game resuming at 5:05 p.m. in the fifth inning. But perhaps the most notable troll came Friday night after the Mets' 4-1 win over the Washington Nationals .

 After the win, which came against the Commanders' neighbor in MLB, the Mets posted a graphic saying they "Stopped at 4 out of respect for Jayden Daniels."

 

 As of Saturday, the post had over 8,700 retweets and 108,000 likes. The Mets rank 22nd in MLB with 514 runs scored.
